discrepancies.where: issues.md, I-49, item 2, third sentence
discrepancies.quote: Non-CpG methylation does rise with the level (Spearman 0.82 in each cohort), so whatever raises the level of a library also leaves a small trace outside CpG context.
discrepancies.problem: The two values are 0.82 and 0.83, and they are for CHH only. In the heat cohort the correlation leans on the two acute heat shock triploids, whose non-CpG methylation is distinctly lower than that of the other eight libraries. The inference of a trace 'outside CpG context' is not the only reading: calls at positions that are CpG in the animal but not in the reference give the same correlation.
discrepancies.evidence: level_correlations.csv: Spearman 0.818182 (heat cohort), 0.825175 (control cohort), reproduced in 01_numbers.out. CHH of zr3534_9 and zr3534_10 is 0.481% and 0.475% against 0.512% to 0.527% in the other eight heat libraries (CHG 0.451% and 0.442% against 0.480% to 0.501%); without these two the heat-cohort Spearman is 0.64 (p = 0.096). Mean CHH of the five high libraries minus mean of the other 17: 0.020 points, against 1.17 points in CpG context.
discrepancies.proposed_text: Non-CpG methylation does rise with the level (CHH: Spearman 0.82 in the heat cohort and 0.83 in the control cohort; `level_correlations.csv`). In the heat cohort part of this comes from the two acute heat shock triploids, zr3534_9 and zr3534_10, whose CHH methylation (0.48% and 0.47%) lies below the 0.51% to 0.53% of the other eight; without them the correlation is 0.64 (p = 0.10). The five high libraries exceed the other 17 by 0.02 points in CHH methylation on average (`04_output/02_alignment_qc/tables/bismark_by_library.csv`), so whatever raises the level of a library leaves at most a small trace in the calls made outside CpG context, and calls at positions that are CpG in the animal but not in the reference could account for it.

challenges.claim: Item 1 and item 2: the 'level' is a property of what the library measures (higher methylation at the same CpGs), not explained by technical quantities.
challenges.objection: (b)1. The level could be an artifact of sequencing depth, duplication, mapping efficiency or coverage at the tested CpGs.
challenges.test_done: 02_alt1_artifacts.R. Within each cohort, Spearman and Pearson correlation of the genome-wide level and of the mean over eligible CpGs with 13 quantities from bismark_by_library.csv and library_coverage.csv and from the per-library coverage of united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz (raw counts reconstructed with the scaling factors of library_filtering_legacy.csv): read pairs, unique pairs, mapping efficiency, duplication, total C, CpGs at 10x, mean genome coverage, mean coverage at tested and at eligible CpGs, ratio of coverage at methylated (mean 90% or more) to unmethylated (10% or less) CpGs, shares of ambiguous and unaligned pairs, level before deduplication. Exact Wilcoxon tests of high against other libraries within cohort.
challenges.result: Heat cohort (n = 10) and control cohort (n = 12), Spearman with the genome-wide level: read pairs 0.35 and -0.01; duplication 0.14 and -0.33; mapping efficiency -0.37 and 0.33; CpGs at 10x 0.42 and -0.07; coverage at tested CpGs -0.19 and -0.18; at eligible CpGs 0.03 and -0.03. Largest absolute values: share of ambiguous pairs -0.55 (heat, p = 0.10) and coverage ratio methylated over unmethylated 0.57 (control, p = 0.055; -0.27 in the heat cohort). None of 26 tests below 0.05. High against other libraries: all exact Wilcoxon p at or above 0.061. Level before and after deduplication correlate 0.993 and the same five libraries are the highest before deduplication. The five high libraries include the control library with the fewest reads (zr3644_14, 36.2 M pairs) and the one with the most (zr3644_15, 58.1 M).

challenges.claim: Item 2: 'Incomplete bisulfite conversion does not explain the level.'
challenges.objection: (b)7. The argument rests on non-CpG methylation as a measure of non-conversion; it could fail if the numbers are wrong or if non-conversion in CpG context differs.
challenges.test_done: 01_numbers.R and 02_alt1_artifacts.R. Recomputed CHG and CHH percentages from the counts of bismark_by_library.csv. As an independent control, pooled methylation of the 363 tested CpGs on the mitochondrial genome (NC_001276.1) per library from united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz. Profile of the excess of the high libraries across classes of CpGs defined by mean methylation in the libraries of the other cohort that are not high.
challenges.result: The bound holds: CHH spans 0.053 points over the 22 libraries and the five high libraries exceed the other 17 by 0.020 points in CHH against 1.17 points in CpG context. Mitochondrial CpGs: heat cohort 0.34%, 0.36% and 0.42% in the three high libraries against 0.33% to 0.62% in the other seven; control cohort 2.9% and 2.4% against 2.0% to 3.6% in the other ten. Excess of the high libraries by class of CpG (heat cohort, control cohort): at or below 1% methylation 0.20 and 0.14 points; 1% to 10%: 2.2 and 1.8; 10% to 30%: 7.4 and 8.9; 30% to 50%: 8.7 and 8.4; 50% to 70%: 7.9 and 6.9; 70% to 90%: 4.9 and 4.0; 90% to 99%: 1.4 and 1.3. Non-conversion would add most at unmethylated CpGs; the excess there is the smallest. The argument is sound. The three wording errors of the item (context label, 0.82 in each cohort, 1 to 2 points) are listed under discrepancies.

challenges.claim: Item 1, heading and correlations: 'that level is the main axis of variation among them'; the genome-wide level 'correlates 0.93 with the first principal component ... and 0.97 with the mean over the eligible CpGs'.
challenges.objection: The correlations could be produced by the five high libraries against the rest, with no graded axis among the other libraries.
challenges.test_done: 09_summaries.R: Pearson and Spearman correlation of the genome-wide level with PC1 (pca_scores_10x_legacy.csv) and with the mean over eligible CpGs (library_level.csv) among the 17 libraries that are not high, and without zr3644_1.
challenges.result: All 22: 0.935 (PC1) and 0.970 (eligible mean), Spearman 0.73 and 0.75. The 17 not high: Pearson 0.58 and 0.78, Spearman 0.41 (p = 0.11) and 0.47 (p = 0.06). Without zr3644_1, the lowest library: Pearson 0.22 and 0.57, Spearman 0.29 and 0.36. PC1 holds 9.47% of the variance (pca_variance.csv). The first component is the contrast of the five high libraries (and zr3644_1 at the other end) with the rest, not a graded axis.
challenges.proposed_text: Add after '(`level_correlations.csv`)': Both correlations are those of the five against the other 17: among the 17 libraries that are not high the genome-wide level correlates 0.58 with the first principal component and 0.78 with the mean over the eligible CpGs (Spearman 0.41 and 0.47), and 0.22 and 0.57 without zr3644_1, the lowest library (verification scripts of check S2-I49, `09_summaries.out`).

challenges.claim: Item 1: the five 'are found by a rule that ignores the group labels: the libraries above the largest gap in the sorted genome-wide values (10.41% to 11.02%)'; title and 'Why it matters': a level difference 'which sits in five libraries'.
challenges.objection: (b)4. Other label-free rules might pick other libraries, and the gap might be a feature of this sample of 22: in the 24 libraries of the control project the values could form a continuum with a tail.
challenges.test_done: 05_alt4_gap_rule.R on the 22 genome-wide values and on the eligible-CpG means: largest and second largest gap, exact one-dimensional k-means (k = 2, 3), normal mixtures by EM (1 to 3 components, BIC), top quartile, Tukey fence, median + 3 MAD. Level of all 24 libraries of project zr3644 from 03_input_files/bismark_reports/061021-big_bismark_summary_report.txt (the 12 of the study agree exactly with bismark_by_library.csv). Parametric bootstrap (20,000 samples of 22) of the largest gap under a normal and a shifted log-normal fitted to the 22 values.
challenges.result: On the 22 values k-means with two clusters, both two-component mixtures and the Tukey fence (10.96%) pick the same five; BIC prefers two components (35.6 against 41.9). The top quartile picks six (adds zr3644_16, 10.41%); median + 3 MAD picks two (zr3534_3, zr3644_14); the second largest gap (0.46 points, between 11.09% and 11.55%) lies inside the five and is three quarters of the largest (0.61). On the eligible means the gaps are 5.07 and 4.56 points (17, then 3, then 2 libraries). Project zr3644: the 12 libraries not in the study run from 9.65% to 10.70%, three of them above 10.41% (10.44%, 10.61%, 10.70%); among the 24 the largest gap (0.58) is between zr3644_15 (11.04%) and zr3644_14 (11.61%), so the gap rule marks zr3644_14 alone, and BIC no longer prefers two components of equal variance (31.5 against 31.8). With the ten heat libraries added (34) the largest gap (0.46) marks zr3534_3 and zr3644_14; the five come out of the second gap (0.32), of k-means with three clusters and of the Tukey fence. A largest gap of 0.61 or more occurs in 18% (normal) to 35% (shifted log-normal) of simulated samples of 22. Shapiro-Wilk on the 22 values p = 0.011 (right-skewed).
challenges.proposed_text: Replace 'They are found by a rule ... in the mean over eligible CpGs.' with: They are the five highest of the 22, found by a rule that ignores the group labels: the libraries above the largest gap in the sorted genome-wide values (10.41% to 11.02%, 0.61 points). The same five lie above the largest gap in the mean over eligible CpGs, and k-means with two clusters, a two-component normal mixture and Tukey's fence pick the same five. They are the upper end of a skewed distribution more than a class of their own. The second largest gap (0.46 points) lies inside the five, between zr3534_5 (11.09%) and zr3534_3 (11.55%). The 12 libraries of project zr3644 that are not part of this study reach 10.44%, 10.61% and 10.70% (`03_input_files/bismark_reports/061021-big_bismark_summary_report.txt`), so that among the 24 libraries of that project the largest gap (0.58 points) sets apart zr3644_14 alone and zr3644_15 stands 0.34 points above the next library. A largest gap of 0.61 points or more occurs in 18% to 35% of samples of 22 drawn from a normal or a shifted log-normal distribution fitted to the 22 values (verification scripts of check S2-I49, `05_alt4_gap_rule.out`).

challenges.claim: Item 3 and 'What would settle it': 'Figure 1B is these five libraries'; the interaction 'comes from the diploid heat group holding three of the five and the triploid control group holding the other two'; 'state that the interaction rests on five libraries'.
challenges.objection: If the interaction were these five libraries it should vanish when they are set aside.
challenges.test_done: 01_numbers.R and 10_followups.R: two-way ANOVA (ploidy by treatment) of the genome-wide level (bismark_by_library.csv, after and before deduplication) on all 22 libraries and on the 17 that are not high; exact enumeration of the interaction contrast over the 21 x 210 = 4,410 regroupings of the 17 within cohort; exact Wilcoxon tests within cohort; the same ANOVA on the mean over eligible CpGs.
challenges.result: Interaction contrast (heat-cohort ploidy difference minus control-cohort ploidy difference): -1.50 points with 22 libraries (F(1,18) = 16.16, p = 0.0008), -0.57 points with 17 (F(1,13) = 6.79, p = 0.022; 32 of 4,410 regroupings as large). Before deduplication: F(1,18) = 14.25 and F(1,13) = 4.77, p = 0.048. Among the 17, D11 and D12 (10.24%, 10.21%) lie above all five heat triploids (9.81% to 10.19%; exact Wilcoxon p = 0.095, the smallest value 2 against 5 can give) and the four control triploids (10.18% to 10.41%) above most control diploids (9.46% to 10.23%; p = 0.038). Mean over eligible CpGs: F(1,18) = 11.49 with 22, F(1,13) = 2.78, p = 0.12 with 17. Removing the highest values of the two higher groups biases against an interaction, so the remainder is not an artifact of the removal. About 62% of the contrast is carried by the five libraries; a smaller interaction remains in the quantity the figure plots.
challenges.proposed_text: Item 3: *Figure 1B is mostly these five libraries.* The ploidy by heat interaction in percent CpG methylation (F(1,18) = 14.49 in the draft; I-01) comes mostly from the diploid heat group holding three of the five and the triploid control group holding the other two: the interaction contrast (ploidy difference of the heat cohort minus that of the control cohort) is -1.50 points with all 22 libraries and -0.57 points with the five set aside. The smaller contrast is still nominally significant in the genome-wide values that the figure plots (F(1,13) = 6.79, p = 0.022; 32 of the 4,410 regroupings of the 17 libraries within cohort give a contrast as large), because D11 and D12 lie above all five heat triploids (10.24% and 10.21% against 9.81% to 10.19%) and the four other control triploids lie above most control diploids (10.18% to 10.41% against 9.46% to 10.23%; exact Wilcoxon p = 0.038). It is not significant in the mean over the eligible CpGs (F(1,13) = 2.78, p = 0.12). Setting the five aside was decided after seeing the data, so these values are exploratory (`library_level.csv`; verification scripts of check S2-I49, `01_numbers.out` and `10_followups.out`). What would settle it: Without new data: show the individual libraries in Figure 1B, state that most of the interaction rests on five libraries, two of them untreated (interaction contrast -1.50 points with all 22 libraries, -0.57 points without the five), and do not interpret lists of loci.

challenges.claim: Item 4: 'How strongly a CpG follows the level, estimated among the libraries of one cohort, predicts the ploidy difference of the other cohort' (47% against 1% in the top tenth).
challenges.objection: (b)5. CpGs with a high variance among animals have both large slopes and large differences, so the association could arise with no level effect; and 'follows the level' suggests a graded dependence that may not exist.
challenges.test_done: 06_alt5_slope_permutation.R and 10_followups.R, eligible CpGs, legacy mode. Decile table recomputed (reproduces level_slope_deciles.csv). Level values permuted among the 12 control libraries (500 random permutations) and among the 10 heat libraries (500), decile shares recomputed each time; permutations classified by the rank of the value given to zr3644_14. Exhaustive variant: each of the 66 pairs of control libraries declared 'high' (slope = pair mean minus mean of the other ten). Slope estimated among the ten control libraries that are not high (300 permutations as reference). Control-cohort slope against the difference between D11, D12 and the five heat triploids.
challenges.result: Observed top tenth: 46.5% diploids higher, 1.1% triploids higher; bottom tenth 10.2% and 5.9%; Spearman -0.365. Permuted level (control cohort): top tenth diploid-higher share median 14.7% (5th to 95th percentile 10.8% to 41.9%), bottom tenth median 15.2%, against 15.6% of all eligible CpGs; 6 of 500 permutations reach the observed share and 1 of 500 the observed Spearman. The asymmetry therefore disappears, and it returns only when a large value falls on zr3644_14: median 37.7% in the 88 permutations that give that library one of the two largest values, 14.5% and 12.2% in the other two classes; 57 of the 63 permutations above 30% are of the first class. Pairs of control libraries: zr3644_14 with zr3644_15 gives 49.7% (rank 1 of 66), any pair with zr3644_14 39% to 43%, the 45 pairs without either 10.6% to 16.2%. Slope among the ten control libraries not high: top tenth 14.6% (permutation range 11.7% to 17.5%), Spearman -0.03. Control-cohort slope against D11, D12 versus the five triploids: top tenth 5.3% and 3.1%, Spearman -0.01. Reverse direction (slope in the heat cohort, control-cohort difference): top tenth 7.2% triploids higher against a permutation median of 5.3% (21 of 500 at least as large), Spearman 0.30 (0 of 500). So the sign claim stands and is not a variance effect; but the 'slope on the level' is in effect the contrast between the two high control libraries (zr3644_14 above all) and the other ten, and no graded dependence on the level is shown.
challenges.proposed_text: Add after the decile sentence: The slope estimated in the control cohort is in effect the contrast between that cohort's two high libraries and its other ten. With the level values permuted among the 12 control libraries, the top tenth of the slope holds a median of 15% of CpGs with the diploids higher in the heat cohort (500 permutations; 5th to 95th percentile 11% to 42%; 6 reach the observed 47%), about the 16% of all eligible CpGs, and the asymmetry returns only when a large value falls on zr3644_14 (median 38% in the 88 permutations that give it one of the two largest values, 15% and 12% in the others). So the association is not a by-product of variable CpGs having both large slopes and large differences. It is also not a graded dependence on the level: among the ten control libraries that are not high the slope predicts nothing (15% in the top tenth; permutation range 12% to 18%). What the analysis shows is that the CpGs at which zr3644_14 and zr3644_15 exceed the other control libraries are the CpGs at which the heat diploids exceed the heat triploids (verification scripts of check S2-I49, `06_alt5_slope_permutation.out` and `10_followups.out`).

challenges.claim: 'Why it matters', second bullet: 'A contrast driven by level lists the CpGs most sensitive to level. This is why DML lie where methylation is intermediate and variable among animals, and why the functions assigned to them reflect which genes have such CpGs (I-41, I-03).'
challenges.objection: The draft's two DML lists come from contrasts that are balanced for the five high libraries (three and two on either side), so they may not be driven by the level at all; I-41 already explains the location of DML by the 20-point rule under any grouping.
challenges.test_done: 07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.R and 08_title_scope.R, legacy mode. Slope of every CpG on the level over all 22 libraries (values and level centred within cohort); share of the draft's eligible ploidy DML, heat DML and shared loci (q < 0.01 and more than 20 points in diffmeth_{ploidy,heat}_legacy.csv.gz) in each tenth of that slope, against lists from 200 random relabellings of ploidy within cohort and against the within-cohort lists. Then the draft's two contrasts recomputed without the five high libraries, and without every other choice of three heat diploids and two control triploids (149 choices): share of the draft's CpGs still above 20 points with the same sign. One library left out at a time.
challenges.result: Level difference between the groups of the draft's contrasts: -0.03 points (ploidy), +0.06 points (cohort). Share in the top tenth of the slope: ploidy DML 3.3% of 1,037, heat DML 3.0% of 2,350, shared loci 3.5% of 200, where 10% of eligible CpGs lie by construction; relabelled lists median 3.9% (0.49 to 0.55 only when all five high libraries fall in one group). For comparison the within-cohort lists: heat cohort 37.8%, control cohort 24.6%. Without the five high libraries 633 of the 1,038 ploidy CpGs (61%) and 1,776 of the 2,352 cohort CpGs (76%) remain; other choices of three heat diploids and two control triploids keep 57% to 74% (median 66%; the five rank 18th of 150) and 65% to 81% (median 73%; the five rank 116th). No single library carries either list (78% to 94% and 83% to 91% remain). Of the 1,038 ploidy CpGs, 880 exceed 20 points with the same sign inside the heat cohort, 776 for D11 and D12 against the five heat triploids, 335 inside the control cohort. The draft's lists are thus depleted of level-sensitive CpGs and do not depend on the five libraries; the sentence misattributes the location and functions of the DML to the level.
challenges.proposed_text: - The level does not explain the draft's own DML lists. The draft's two contrasts are balanced for the five high libraries (three and two on either side; the level differs by -0.03 points between the ploidy groups and by +0.06 points between the cohorts, `level_group_tests.csv`), and level-sensitive CpGs cancel in them: 3% of the draft's ploidy DML and 3% of its heat DML lie in the top tenth of the slope on the level, where 10% of the eligible CpGs lie by construction, and without the five libraries 61% of the 1,038 ploidy CpGs and 76% of the 2,352 cohort CpGs stay above 20 points with the same sign, as many as when any other three heat diploids and two control triploids are left out (57% to 74% and 65% to 81%; verification scripts of check S2-I49, `07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.out` and `08_title_scope.out`). Why DML lie where methylation is intermediate and variable among animals, and why the functions assigned to them reflect which genes have such CpGs, is explained in I-41 and I-03: the 20-point rule selects such CpGs under any grouping. What the level does explain is the direction of the contrasts inside each cohort and of the interaction (item 4), and most of the interaction of Figure 1B (item 3).

challenges.claim: Item 6: 'The five triploids of the heat cohort resemble each other more than any other five libraries of that cohort do' (ten highest of 45 pairs; mean 0.929, rank 1 of 252).
challenges.objection: (b)2. Pairwise Pearson correlation falls with binomial sampling noise; the triploid libraries might simply have more reads at the tested CpGs.
challenges.test_done: 03_alt23_similarity.R. Raw counts reconstructed from united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz and the scaling factors (exact for all ten heat libraries). Mean raw coverage per library at tested and eligible CpGs; Spearman of the 45 pairwise correlations with the mean, harmonic-mean and inverse coverage of the pair. Thinning: every heat library subsampled without replacement to the minimum coverage of the ten at each CpG (median 17 reads), 8 seeds, and to exactly 10 reads at every CpG, 4 seeds; correlations, rank of the triploid subset among 252, number of triploid pairs among the ten highest. Noise-corrected correlations (binomial sampling variance removed from each library's variance), no random draw.
challenges.result: Mean raw coverage at the tested CpGs: 34.8 reads (triploids) against 35.3 (diploids); at eligible CpGs 32.3 against 32.4. zr3534_7 has the fewest reads of the cohort and the highest correlation (0.937 with zr3534_9). Pairwise r against pair coverage: Spearman 0.05 (p = 0.76); against the difference in level: -0.80. Thinned to equal coverage: rank 1 of 252 in 8 of 8 seeds, all ten triploid pairs the ten highest in each, mean 0.916 against 0.911 for the best other subset; thinned to 10 reads: rank 1 in 4 of 4 seeds (0.892 against 0.887). Noise-corrected: triploid pairs 0.949 to 0.965, all other pairs at or below 0.936. On each of the ten chromosomes the triploid subset is rank 1 of 252.

challenges.claim: Item 6 (same statement), read as a feature separate from the level, and item 5: D11 and D12 'still differ from the five triploids at more CpGs than any other pair of those seven libraries does'.
challenges.objection: (b)3. The similarity could be a consequence of the level: the three high diploids lower the diploid correlations, and pairs with similar level correlate more.
challenges.test_done: 03_alt23_similarity.R and 04_cross_cohort_similarity.R. Ranking of the 21 pairs among the seven heat libraries that are not high (step 04 values and noise-corrected). Level removed from the heat libraries with slopes estimated in the control cohort (so that the heat-cohort grouping cannot be absorbed), then correlations and rank. Regression of the 45 pairwise r on the difference in level and a triploid-pair indicator.
challenges.result: Among the seven, the ten triploid pairs hold ranks 1 to 10 of 21 (0.922 to 0.937), the ten diploid-triploid pairs ranks 11 to 20 (0.907 to 0.913), and D11 with D12 is the least similar pair (0.906, rank 21 of 21; rank 25 of the 45 pairs of the cohort), although D11, D12 and T11 have almost the same level (10.24%, 10.21%, 10.19%). After removal of the level with control-cohort slopes: triploid subset rank 1 of 252, ten of the ten highest pairs. Regression: -0.020 per point of level difference (t = -9.7) and +0.019 for triploid pairs (t = 7.4). The similarity is not a consequence of the level. The pair D11, D12 is unusual in the opposite sense to a group: the two share nothing that sets them apart together, so the 1 of 21 of item 5 reflects the five triploids being alike, not the two diploids being alike. (A regression on the level fitted inside the heat cohort gives rank 231, but there level and ploidy are collinear and the fit absorbs the group difference; that variant is not a valid test.)

challenges.claim: Item 6, reading: 'The control cohort has no such structure'; 'A group of mutually similar libraries is what related animals (one cross), one processing batch, or a common biological state would each produce'; and 'Why it matters' (b): 'a set of five triploid libraries that resemble each other'.
challenges.objection: The triploids may not be a special group at all: they may simply share the profile common to most libraries, including those of the other experiment, while each heat diploid departs from it. The comparison of 0.929 with 0.908 to 0.912 in the control cohort is confounded by coverage (control libraries have fewer reads).
challenges.test_done: 04_cross_cohort_similarity.R, 09_summaries.R, 11_library_order.R. Cross-cohort correlations in library_correlation_10x_legacy.csv and _corrected.csv (no thinning). All 22 libraries thinned to the minimum coverage of the 22 at each CpG (median 11 reads; mean of 5 seeds) and noise-corrected correlations; average-linkage clustering on 1 - r; mean correlation of each library that is not high with the other 16.
challenges.result: Step 04 values, both modes: every heat triploid correlates more with every one of the 12 control libraries than D11 or D12 does (120 of 120 comparisons); each heat triploid correlates more with the ten control libraries that are not high (means 0.913 to 0.917) than with D11 and D12 (0.907 to 0.913), in spite of the lower coverage of the control libraries. At equal coverage: heat triploids among themselves 0.903 (0.898 to 0.912); the ten control libraries not high among themselves 0.901 (0.863 to 0.926); seven of them (zr3644_3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 16, 18; four diploids, three triploids) 0.916 (0.911 to 0.926); heat triploids with the ten control libraries 0.894; D11 and D12 with the heat triploids 0.887, with the ten control libraries 0.884, with each other 0.883. Noise-corrected: 0.954, 0.948, 0.965, 0.943, 0.934, 0.930, 0.928. Clustering joins the five heat triploids with eight control libraries (the seven and zr3644_15) before D11 or D12 join anything. Among the 17 libraries not high, the four least like the others are zr3644_1, zr3534_2 (D12), zr3534_1 (D11) and zr3644_2, that is the libraries numbered 1 and 2 of each project (exact Wilcoxon against the other 13, p = 0.0008; a comparison made after seeing the data). So the heat triploids are no more alike than ordinary control libraries are, and they resemble the control libraries of another experiment more than they resemble the diploids of their own; what is particular to the heat cohort is that all five diploids lie outside the common profile.
challenges.proposed_text: Replace from 'The five diploids are no more similar' to 'would each produce.' with: The five diploids are no more similar to each other (0.898) than to the triploids (0.898); D11 and D12, the two diploids with an ordinary level, are the least similar pair among the seven libraries of the cohort that are not high (0.906, below each of their correlations with a triploid, 0.907 to 0.913). In the control cohort similarity does not follow ploidy: 0.912 among diploids, 0.908 among triploids, 0.908 between. These values cannot be set beside the 0.929 of the heat triploids, because the control libraries have fewer reads and a correlation falls with sampling noise. With every library thinned to the same number of reads at each CpG, the five heat triploids correlate at 0.903 on average, the ten control libraries that are not high at 0.901, and seven of these (zr3644_3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 16 and 18, of both ploidies) at 0.916. The heat triploids are therefore as similar to each other as ordinary libraries of the control cohort are, and they resemble those libraries too: each heat triploid correlates more with every one of the 12 control libraries than D11 or D12 does (120 of 120 comparisons in `library_correlation_10x_legacy.csv`), and more with the ten control libraries that are not high (0.913 to 0.917 on average) than with D11 and D12 (0.907 to 0.913). What is particular to the heat cohort is that all five diploids lie outside this common profile, three by their level and two in ways they do not share with each other, while all five triploids lie inside it. Read depth does not produce this: the triploid libraries have no more reads at the tested CpGs than the diploid ones (34.8 against 35.3 per CpG on average), and after thinning the triploids remain the most similar of the 252 subsets of five in each of eight draws. A profile shared with animals of another experiment does not call for one cross or one processing batch among the triploids. The open question is what sets the five diploids of the heat experiment apart: their source, the handling of their libraries, or their response to heat (verification scripts of check S2-I49, `03_alt23_similarity.out`, `04_cross_cohort_similarity.out` and `09_summaries.out`).

challenges.claim: 'Why it matters', first bullet: 'What the draft reads as ploidy-specific responses to heat ... is, in these data, two things: (a) ... which sits in five libraries, and (b) a set of five triploid libraries that resemble each other. Neither has been shown to be a property of ploidy or an effect of heat.' Also item 2, last sentence (causes of the level).
challenges.objection: (b)6. The draft's own hypothesis (heat changed methylation in diploids and not in triploids) would produce exactly this picture: three of five heat diploids with a raised level, triploids uniform and unchanged. 'Is ... two things' and the list of causes in item 2 leave that reading out.
challenges.test_done: Collected from 01, 04, 07, 09, 10 and 11: within-cohort level tests, cross-cohort similarity, ELISA rank tests, Fisher exact tests of the frequency of high libraries (heat cohort against control cohort and against all 24 libraries of project zr3644), acute heat shock by ploidy (linear model on the ten heat libraries).
challenges.result: For the hypothesis: all five heat diploids exceed all five heat triploids in level (p = 0.008); the ELISA, the one assay with the heat experiment's own controls, shows the rise in diploids (exact Wilcoxon heat against control diploids p = 0.010; heat diploids against heat triploids p = 0.050; triploids heat against control p = 0.16); the heat triploids look like untreated libraries of the other experiment while every heat diploid departs from that profile; both acute heat shock diploids are high (2 of 2 against 1 of 3 without it; acute by ploidy interaction not testable, p = 0.32). Against it: the raised level occurs without heat, in 2 of 12 control libraries (2 of the 24 of project zr3644), with the same CpG profile (item 4), and its frequency is not demonstrably higher after heat (3 of 10 against 2 of 12, Fisher exact p = 0.62; against 2 of 24, p = 0.14); only three of five heat diploids show it; D11 and D12 depart from the common profile in ways they do not share (least similar pair), which is not what a common response gives, and two control libraries numbered 1 and 2 depart in the same manner without heat; the ELISA and the WGBS differ in size (80% against 9% excess of heat diploids over heat triploids) and agree in the six shared animals only through D13. The data cannot exclude the hypothesis and cannot support it beyond the ELISA. 'Neither has been shown to be ...' is correct; 'is, in these data, two things' and item 2's list of causes are firmer than that.
challenges.proposed_text: First bullet: - Inside the heat cohort the difference between diploids and triploids consists, in these data, of two things: (a) a higher overall methylation level in the diploids, most of which sits in three libraries, and (b) five triploid libraries that resemble each other and most control libraries, against five diploid libraries that each lie outside that common profile. Neither has been shown to be a property of ploidy or an effect of heat, and neither is excluded as one. A response to heat confined to the diploids, which is what the draft proposes, would produce both; so would five diploid animals that differed from the others before the treatment, or libraries that differ through their preparation. The WGBS data cannot tell these apart, because the control animals of the heat experiment were not sequenced (I-01). What they do show is that (a) is not specific to heat: two of the six untreated triploids of the control cohort, which belongs to another experiment, carry the same raised level at the same CpGs (item 4), so that the level difference between ploidy groups has the opposite sign there, and libraries with a raised level are not demonstrably more frequent after heat (3 of 10 heat libraries against 2 of the 12 control libraries, Fisher exact p = 0.62; against 2 of the 24 libraries of project zr3644, p = 0.14). Item 2, last sentence: Whether the cause is biological (animals or tissue samples that are more methylated, or, for the three heat diploids, a response to the treatment) or lies in library preparation cannot be decided from these data.

challenges.claim: Item 7 of I-49, through its references: I-08, update of 2026-11-19: a group uniformly different from every other animal 'is the pattern a shared allele or sequence variant gives, and not what ploidy or heat would give'; I-06, item 6: such a CpG 'is what an allele or a sequence variant shared by related animals produces in bisulfite data'.
challenges.objection: (b)6. A response to heat confined to one ploidy, the draft's hypothesis, gives exactly this pattern: the heat triploids (or the heat diploids) are the only group with their combination of ploidy and treatment. Only main effects are excluded by the pattern.
challenges.test_done: Read corrected_dml_library_values.csv and corrected_dml_group_apart.csv; read the counts at NC_047565.1:35,030,701 and its tested neighbours within 2 kb in united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz (07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.R and a direct read of the table).
challenges.result: At NC_047565.1:35,030,701 the heat triploids are at 10/16, 11/24, 12/32, 10/24, 11/31 methylated reads and 16 of the other 17 libraries at 0 (D12 2/29). The tested CpG 16 bp away (35,030,717) shows the same: 16/20, 13/24, 14/33, 13/28, 11/32 against 0 in 15 libraries and 1 read in two. A single C/T substitution would not affect two CpGs; a haplotype with its own methylation shared by related triploids would, and so would methylation of this stretch in response to heat in triploids. Values near one third to two thirds fit one or two of three alleles. Of the 125 CpGs of the heat-cohort list 11 have the triploids apart and 6 the diploids apart. The data do not decide between an allele and a ploidy-specific response; the I-08 sentence excludes the second more firmly than they allow.
challenges.proposed_text: I-08, update: A group of animals that is uniformly different from every other animal, controls of the same ploidy included, is the pattern a shared allele or sequence variant gives. A main effect of ploidy or of heat would not give it; a response to heat confined to one ploidy would, because each of these two groups is the only one with its combination of ploidy and treatment. I-06, item 6, add after '(I-08, I-49).': A response to heat confined to the triploids would look the same in these data; at this locus the tested CpG 16 bp away shows the same pattern (34% to 80% in the five heat-cohort triploids, 0% to 6% in the other 17 libraries), which a single base substitution would not produce.

challenges.claim: I-01, update of 2026-11-19: 'The ploidy contrast is balanced in numbers only. ... among the heat-treated libraries diploids and triploids differ, among the controls they do not ... The pooled ploidy contrast of the draft averages two unlike things.' and 'Option 3 loses most of its content. ... It does not replicate.'
challenges.objection: (b)6. A ploidy difference present after heat and absent in controls is the draft's interaction hypothesis; failure to replicate among untreated animals is what that hypothesis predicts, so the wording should not read as evidence against it.
challenges.test_done: Recomputed the numbers of the two bullets (01_numbers.R): correlation of the two within-cohort differences, counts above 20 points in both cohorts and with the same sign, with and without the five libraries.
challenges.result: -0.3003 (all tested CpGs, Pearson); 969 in both, 181 with the same sign (18.7%); without the five -0.0359 (all tested CpGs; -0.0295 eligible), 923 and 407 (44.1%; 48% expected from the two direction shares of 41% and 61% triploid higher). All reproduce except the rounding of -0.04 (see discrepancies). The statements are correct as descriptions; neither bullet says that the pattern is also what a response to heat that differs by ploidy would give. 'Among the controls they do not' is true of counts and p-values at single CpGs and sits beside a level difference with p = 0.009.
challenges.proposed_text: Second bullet, add at the end: A ploidy difference that is present among the heat-treated animals and absent among the controls is also what the draft's hypothesis of a ploidy-specific response to heat predicts; because treatment and experiment coincide, these data cannot tell such a response from a difference between the two sets of animals (I-49). Third bullet, replace 'It does not replicate.' with: It does not replicate. That rules out a ploidy difference common to both experiments; it says nothing about a difference that heat brings out, which could not replicate among untreated animals.

challenges.claim: I-06, 'What follows for the manuscript', third bullet: 'I-49 describes the difference: three diploid libraries with a higher overall methylation level, and five triploid libraries that resemble each other. Whether heat produced it cannot be decided without WGBS of that experiment's own control animals.'
challenges.objection: (b)6. Does this paragraph exclude the draft's hypothesis more firmly than the data allow?
challenges.test_done: Read the three bullets against the tables: dml_counts.csv (12,405 and 125), relabelling_reference.csv (13,028, 2 of 252).
challenges.result: Numbers reproduce (12,405; 125; 13,028 the largest of 252, shared with its mirror image). The bullet leaves the cause open in so many words. Nothing to change for the hypothesis; if the rewording of item 6 of I-49 is adopted, 'five triploid libraries that resemble each other' should follow it.

challenges.claim: 'Why it matters', third bullet: 'The two assays agree in direction for the heat-treated animals. They cannot confirm each other, for two reasons.'
challenges.objection: (b)8. Half of the heat-treated diploid ELISA values are extrapolated above the highest standard used, so the direction might rest on unreliable values; and 'cannot confirm each other' passes over the fact that the ELISA has the experiment's own controls.
challenges.test_done: 07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.R on elisa_percent_5mC.csv, group_summary.csv, elisa_standard_curve.csv and pct_mCpG_by_library.csv: group means; values capped at the highest standard used in the fit (absorbance 0.826, equal to 3.94% 5-mC); exact Wilcoxon tests; Spearman and Pearson correlation in the six animals with both measurements, with and without D13; ratio of group means in both assays.
challenges.result: Group means reproduce: 4.02, 2.23, 1.70, 1.68. Four of the eight heat-treated diploids are flagged above_top_standard (D13 to D16; the task text says three, which is the number Figure 1A drops, I-11). Capped at the top standard the heat-treated diploid mean is 3.27 against 2.23. Ranks do not depend on extrapolation: five of eight heat-treated diploids exceed every heat-treated triploid; exact Wilcoxon p = 0.0499; heat against control diploids p = 0.010. Six animals: Spearman 0.543 (p = 0.297), Pearson 0.753 (p = 0.084); without D13, which is the highest in both and one of the four extrapolated values, Spearman 0.20 (p = 0.78). Size: heat-treated diploids over heat-treated triploids 1.80 in the ELISA (1.47 capped) against 1.085 in the WGBS. D19, D20, T19 and T20 have no ELISA value. 'Agree in direction' is fair; the bullet lacks the extrapolation, the difference in size and the dependence on D13, and it understates that the ELISA is evidence in its own right.
challenges.proposed_text: - The ELISA of the heat experiment reports a difference of the same kind as (a): 4.0% 5-mC in heat-treated diploids against 2.2% in heat-treated triploids, and 1.7% in both control groups (`04_output/03_global_methylation/tables/group_summary.csv`; limits of the assay in I-10 and I-12). Four of the eight values of the heat-treated diploids (D13 to D16) lie above the highest standard used in the fit and are extrapolated (`elisa_percent_5mC.csv`), so 4.0% is not a measured mean; with the four set to the value of that standard the mean is 3.3%. The direction does not depend on them: five of the eight heat-treated diploids exceed every heat-treated triploid (exact Wilcoxon p = 0.050). The two assays agree in direction for the heat-treated animals and not in size: the heat-treated diploids exceed the heat-treated triploids by 80% in the ELISA and by 9% in genome-wide CpG methylation. The ELISA is the only methylation measurement that includes the control animals of the heat experiment, and therefore the only evidence for an effect of heat on overall methylation in diploids that is free of the confound of I-01. The WGBS can neither confirm nor contradict it, for two reasons. It has no control animals from the heat experiment, and in the other experiment two of six untreated triploids are as high as the three high heat-treated diploids, so libraries with a high level occur without heat. And only six animals have both an ELISA value and a WGBS library (D11 to D13, T11 to T13): the two measurements correlate at 0.54 (Spearman, p = 0.30), and at 0.20 without D13, which is the highest in both and one of the four extrapolated ELISA values. D19 and D20, two of the three high heat-treated diploids, have no ELISA value.

challenges.claim: Title of I-49 and its row in the summary table: 'The group differences in the WGBS data are carried by five libraries with a higher overall methylation level and by five mutually similar triploid libraries'.
challenges.objection: (c) 'Carried by' should hold for the group differences the draft reports. It may hold for some contrasts only, and the second half may describe the wrong group.
challenges.test_done: Combination of the tests above: leave-five-out and leave-one-out of the draft's two contrasts (08_title_scope.R); interaction of Figure 1B without the five (01, 10); direction shares of all 252 and 21 regroupings (07); cross-cohort similarity (04, 09).
challenges.result: Supported: the direction of the contrasts inside each cohort follows the high libraries (85% one direction with the observed grouping; median 88% over the 42 regroupings that keep the three high heat libraries together, 62% over the other 210), and about 62% of the Figure 1B interaction contrast is theirs. Not supported: (1) the draft's ploidy and heat lists do not depend on the five (61% and 76% remain without them, inside the range for other libraries of the same groups); (2) a smaller level interaction remains among the other 17 (p = 0.022); (3) the five triploids are not a distinctive set (as similar to each other as ordinary control libraries, and closer to the control libraries than to D11 and D12); the distinctive fact is that every heat diploid lies outside the common profile. Without the three high libraries the remaining difference has no preferred direction: 59% with D11 and D12 higher, against 51% to 61% for the other 20 pairs, as I-49 says.
challenges.proposed_text: Title: ### I-49 (S1) Inside the heat cohort the ploidy difference consists of three diploid libraries with a higher overall methylation level and two more diploid libraries of unusual profile, against five triploid libraries that resemble each other and most control libraries; two control triploids have the same raised level, so the level difference has the opposite sign in the control cohort. Summary row: | I-49 | S1 | Interpretation | Inside the heat cohort the ploidy difference consists of three diploid libraries with a higher overall methylation level and two more diploid libraries of unusual profile, against five triploid libraries that resemble each other and most control libraries; two control triploids have the same raised level, so most of the Figure 1B interaction rests on five libraries; the draft's own DML lists do not depend on them; the ploidy difference of one cohort is not found in the other | needs information |

challenges.claim: Severity S1 of I-49 ('a main conclusion of the manuscript depends on it').
challenges.objection: (c) I-49 is a description whose cause is undetermined, and the main conclusions about loci are already removed by I-01, I-02 and I-06; by the definitions it may be S2 ('materially changes how a result should be read').
challenges.test_done: Compared the definitions at the top of issues.md with what the evidence of I-49 bears on, using the results above.
challenges.result: A main conclusion that does depend on I-49 is the reading of Figure 1B (Results 3.1) as a ploidy-specific response of overall methylation to heat: about 62% of that interaction is five libraries, two of them untreated. For the DML lists of Results 3.2 to 3.5 nothing depends on I-49 (they do not depend on the five libraries, and their basis is removed by I-01, I-02 and I-06). S1 is justified for the first and not for the second; the 'Where' line and the title should say so (see discrepancies).
challenges.proposed_text: Add to I-49: **Rating.** S1 for Results 3.1 and the passages of the Discussion that read Figure 1B as a ploidy-specific response to heat: most of that interaction rests on five libraries, two of them from untreated animals. The DML lists of Results 3.2 to 3.5 do not depend on those five libraries; what removes their basis is I-01, I-02 and I-06, and for them this issue only describes what the libraries of the heat cohort look like.

additions.item: The level does not follow sequencing depth, duplication, mapping efficiency or coverage, and is the same before deduplication.
additions.why_it_matters: Item 2 rules out incomplete conversion only. A reader will ask next whether deeper, more duplicated or differently covered libraries are the high ones; the control cohort's high libraries include both its smallest and its largest library.
additions.where_to_add: I-49, item 2, after the sentence on the 0.05-point bound
additions.proposed_text: Nor does the level follow the amount or quality of sequencing. Within each cohort it is unrelated to the number of read pairs (Spearman 0.35 in the heat cohort, -0.01 in the control cohort), the duplication rate (0.14, -0.33), the mapping efficiency (-0.37, 0.33), the number of CpGs with 10x coverage (0.42, -0.07) and the mean coverage at the tested CpGs (-0.19, -0.18); none of 13 such quantities reaches p = 0.05 in either cohort (`04_output/02_alignment_qc/tables/bismark_by_library.csv`, `04_output/04_cpg_coverage/tables/library_coverage.csv`; verification scripts of check S2-I49, `02_level_vs_qc.csv`). The same five libraries are the highest before deduplication (`04_output/03_global_methylation/tables/pct_mCpG_by_library.csv`).

additions.item: Two internal controls that exclude incomplete conversion more directly than non-CpG methylation: the mitochondrial CpGs and the profile of the excess across classes of CpGs.
additions.why_it_matters: Non-CpG methylation measures non-conversion outside CpG context; the mitochondrial CpGs measure it in CpG context, and the class profile shows the excess is smallest exactly where unconverted cytosines would add most.
additions.where_to_add: I-49, item 2, before the last sentence
additions.proposed_text: Two further observations point the same way. The 363 tested CpGs of the mitochondrial genome, which is expected to be unmethylated, are no more methylated in the high libraries than in the others of their cohort (heat cohort: 0.34% to 0.42% in the three high libraries, 0.33% to 0.62% in the other seven; control cohort: 2.4% and 2.9% in the two high libraries, 2.0% to 3.6% in the other ten; the difference between the cohorts at these CpGs is a difference between the two sequencing projects and belongs to I-01). And the excess of the high libraries over the others of their cohort is largest where methylation is intermediate (7 to 9 points at CpGs between 10% and 70%) and smallest at unmethylated CpGs (0.1 to 0.2 points at CpGs at or below 1%), where unconverted cytosines would add most (verification scripts of check S2-I49, `02_alt1_artifacts.out`).

additions.item: Among the 17 libraries that are not high, the four least like the others are the libraries numbered 1 and 2 of each project, which include D11 and D12.
additions.why_it_matters: It gives a third reading of the difference that remains in the heat cohort without the three high libraries (1 of 21): not ploidy and not heat, but something tied to the position of a library in its project, present in the control project as well. It makes the request for the order and batches of library preparation specific. The comparison was made after seeing the data and must be labelled so.
additions.where_to_add: I-49, item 6, at the end; and 'Needs from authors', second bullet
additions.proposed_text: Item 6: Among the 17 libraries that are not high, the four that resemble the others least are the libraries numbered 1 and 2 of each project: zr3644_1, zr3534_2 (D12), zr3534_1 (D11) and zr3644_2 (mean correlation with the other 16 at equal coverage 0.874 to 0.886, against 0.890 to 0.904 for the other 13; exact Wilcoxon p = 0.0008, a comparison made after seeing the data; verification scripts of check S2-I49, `11_library_order.out`). Something tied to the position of a library in its project would therefore account for D11 and D12 as well as ploidy or heat does. Needs from authors, second bullet: The order and batches in which the libraries were prepared, and whether the libraries numbered 1 and 2 of each project (zr3534_1, zr3534_2, zr3644_1, zr3644_2) were handled differently from the rest, for example as a first batch.

additions.item: The draft's Methods say that E. coli amplicons were added to every sample to assess bisulfite conversion efficiency; I-49 does not ask for those values.
additions.why_it_matters: The spike-in gives the conversion rate of each library directly and would close item 2 without argument. It also tests whether zr3534_9 and zr3534_10, whose non-CpG methylation is distinctly lower than that of the other eight heat libraries, were converted separately.
additions.where_to_add: I-49, 'Needs from authors', new bullets
additions.proposed_text:
- The bisulfite conversion efficiency of each library. The Methods of the draft say that E. coli amplicons were added to every sample to assess it; the per-library values from the sequencing provider, or the reads that map to those amplicons, would settle item 2 directly.
- Whether libraries zr3534_9 and zr3534_10 were converted or prepared separately from zr3534_1 to 8: their non-CpG methylation (CHH 0.48% and 0.47%, CHG 0.45% and 0.44%) lies below that of the other eight (CHH 0.51% to 0.53%, CHG 0.48% to 0.50%; `04_output/02_alignment_qc/tables/bismark_by_library.csv`).

additions.item: 'What would settle it' lacks the two checks that separate an animal property from a library artifact and that test relatedness without a pedigree.
additions.why_it_matters: WGBS of the heat experiment's own controls tests the effect of heat but not whether a raised level belongs to the animal or to the library. A second library from the same DNA does that at low cost. Relatedness can be estimated from the existing alignments, so the family question does not have to wait for records.
additions.where_to_add: I-49, 'What would settle it', after 'Variant calls from the alignments (I-08).'
additions.proposed_text: The same variant calls give the pairwise relatedness of the animals, which tests whether the triploids, or the diploids, of the heat experiment are one family without the pedigree. A second library from the DNA of one high and one ordinary animal of each cohort would tell a property of the animal from an artifact of library preparation. Because libraries with a raised level occur in 2 of 12 untreated libraries here (2 of the 24 of project zr3644), WGBS of the control animals of the heat experiment needs more than a few animals per group to show that the level rises with heat.

additions.item: 'Needs from authors' asks about the triploids of the heat experiment only; the group that departs from the common profile is the diploids.
additions.why_it_matters: The first bullet steers the authors to the triploid family question. The cross-cohort comparison shows that the heat triploids are ordinary and that every heat diploid is not, so the source and handling of the diploids, D11 and D12 included, is the more informative question.
additions.where_to_add: I-49, 'Needs from authors', first and third bullets
additions.proposed_text: First bullet: Source and crosses of the diploid and the triploid animals of each experiment. Were the triploids of the heat experiment one family? Did the diploids of the heat experiment come from the same stock as its triploids and as the animals of the control experiment? Third bullet: Anything recorded about animals D11, D12, D13, D19 and D20 and about the animals behind zr3644_14 and zr3644_15: size, sex, gonad stage, condition, position in the sampling order, the time between the acute heat shock and sampling for D19 and D20, and the amount and quality of the DNA that went into each library.

additions.item: The margin by which the observed grouping of the heat cohort is the largest of 252, and what the 85% share reflects.
additions.why_it_matters: '2 of 252' is the floor of the enumeration and reads as a strong result for ploidy. The next regrouping differs by one exchanged pair and 1.6%, and the directional share is common to every regrouping that keeps the three high libraries together, so both numbers mostly restate where the high libraries are.
additions.where_to_add: I-49, item 5, after the table
additions.proposed_text: The observed grouping of the ten heat libraries leads the next one, in which D11 and T11 change places, by 206 CpGs (13,028 against 12,822; `relabelling_small_sets.csv`). The share of 85% in one direction is common to the regroupings that keep the three high libraries together (median 88% over those 21 regroupings and their mirror images, 62% over the other 210; verification scripts of check S2-I49, `07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.out`).

result.notes:
Scripts and outputs (record of this check): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/S2-I49-evidence-and-alternatives/ (00_cache_counts.R; 01_numbers.R/.out; 02_alt1_artifacts.R/.out with 02_level_vs_qc.csv and 02_library_qc.csv; 03_alt23_similarity.R/.out with 03_thinning_heat.csv; 04_cross_cohort_similarity.R/.out with 04_thinned_correlation_22.csv; 05_alt4_gap_rule.R/.out; 06_alt5_slope_permutation.R/.out; 07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.R/.out; 08_title_scope.R/.out; 09_summaries.R/.out; 10_followups.R/.out; 11_library_order.R/.out; I49_snapshot_0905.txt is the text of I-49 that was checked). Nothing under the repository was modified; no outside service was used. All code is my own; no function of the repository was called.

Counting: 136 numbers or statements of I-49, of the I-01 update and of the I-06 'What follows' paragraph were compared with the tables; 122 hold as written. The key numbers named in the task were recomputed independently and reproduce: the five libraries and the gap (0.607, second gap 0.464); heat cohort 13,028 CpGs (1,915 triploid higher, 11,113 diploid higher), control cohort 3,349 (2,688 and 661); correlation of the two within-cohort differences -0.3003; the 21 counts of the two-against-five enumeration (same order, median 7,234, largest other 8,737, observed the largest); mean pairwise correlation of the heat triploids 0.9290, rank 1 of 252; also the Wilcoxon tests, the 252, 924, 210 and 4,410 enumerations and the decile table. My counts use 'absolute difference > 20' with no tolerance and differ from the script's (which requires > 20 + 1e-9) by 0 to 3 CpGs per count (for example 10,733 against 10,732; 1,549 against 1,552 of 4,410); this is the tie rule documented in the script header, not an error.

I-49 was edited by another agent while this check ran (the ELISA bullet now cites group_summary.csv and I-12). All quotes are from the text as it stood at 09:05; the proposed ELISA text builds on that version.

Task wording: the task says three of the eight ELISA diploid heat animals are flagged above the top standard. elisa_percent_5mC.csv flags four (D13 to D16), as I-12 says; three is the number Figure 1A drops (I-11).

Not checked, and why: (1) the 9.5% of variance of PC1 was read from pca_variance.csv (9.47%); my own PCA without step 04's filtering gives 18.7% unscaled and 7.3% scaled, so the value depends on step 04's method, which I did not rerun. (2) Corrected mode was checked by reading the tables and, for the cross-cohort similarity, from library_correlation_10x_corrected.csv (120 of 120 comparisons there too); the other new analyses are legacy mode only. (3) Alignments, raw reads and the spike-in amplicons are not available, so M-bias, insert size, conversion efficiency, variant calls and relatedness could not be examined. (4) Whether library number is the order of processing is not known; the neighbour test of the level along library number is not significant (zr3644, 24 libraries, p = 0.10; zr3534 p = 0.13), and that the high libraries carry consecutive numbers (3, 4, 5 and 14, 15) is unremarkable once they are known to fall in one ploidy block (chance 0.3 and 0.33).

Weak points of my own additions: the observation on the libraries numbered 1 and 2 and the 17-library interaction are post hoc; the 'seven control libraries' were named after looking at the matrix (average-linkage clustering returns them, with zr3644_15, in one cluster with the five heat triploids). The estimate that calls at positions that are CpG in the animal could explain the CHH trend is an order of magnitude only (about 1% of CHH calls would suffice). The regression on the level fitted inside the heat cohort gave rank 231 of 252 for the triploid subset; I judge that variant invalid because level and ploidy are collinear in that cohort, and report the control-cohort-slope adjustment instead (rank 1).

By-products outside I-49: (a) For I-01: the sentence 'Non-CpG methylation is equal, so bisulfite conversion was comparable' holds for CHH (0.51% and 0.50%), but at the 363 tested mitochondrial CpGs pooled methylation is 0.33% to 0.62% in the heat cohort and 1.97% to 3.64% in the control cohort, a sixfold difference between the two projects in a sequence expected to be unmethylated; this bears on the 138 mitochondrial CpGs among the corrected heat calls (I-06, item 6). (b) The profile of the excess of the high libraries is close to a constant shift on the logit scale (odds ratio about 1.4 from CpGs under 1% up to 90%), which fits one factor acting on all CpGs (cell composition, a global change, or preferential recovery of methylated fragments) and neither incomplete conversion nor loss of signal by over-conversion. (c) D12 and D13 share a component that is not the level (PC3 scores 201 and 242; correlation 0.908 against 0.880 for D11 with D13). (d) The sentence of I-08 quoted in the challenges lies outside the three places the task named, but item 7 of I-49 rests on it.

discrepancies.where: issues.md, I-06, Update 2026-11-19, item 1: the heading and the two sentences from 'Binomial reads simulated' to 'at a typical CpG.'
discrepancies.quote: *Variation among animals is about three times what the model assumes.* [...] Binomial reads simulated at the same coverage give 0.98, and 1.18 after the coverage scaling and rounding that step 05 applies, so 1.18 is the value to compare with. The test statistic of the uncorrected model is thus inflated about threefold at a typical CpG.
discrepancies.problem: The uncorrected model assumes a dispersion of 1, not 1.18. methylKit:::logReg sets phi = 1 for overdispersion "none" and refers the deviance difference to chi-squared with 1 degree of freedom whatever the scaling of the counts; 1.18 is what binomial reads give after the scaling of step 05, and the model does not allow for it. The statistic is therefore inflated by the whole observed dispersion (3.67 at the median CpG), not by 3.67 / 1.18 = 3.1. The figure 3.1 is the part that variation among libraries adds. 06_diagnostics/README.md (How to read the size of a list, point 6) says the statistics are 'too large by about the observed dispersion', which contradicts 'about threefold', and its sentence 'The model of the draft assumes the dispersion of the second row, not exactly 1' is wrong in the same way. Also, one library was made per animal, so the excess is variation among libraries; it cannot be assigned to animals as opposed to library preparation.
discrepancies.evidence: Source of methylKit 1.28.0 (01_methylkit_source.out): phi = switch(overdispersion, none = 1, ...), p = pchisq(deviance/phi, 1). On my own sample of 3,000 eligible CpGs of united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz: median dispersion 3.72 (06_sample_and_parity.log); median of the uncorrected statistic over the median of chi-squared(1) = 3.90 with the real ploidy labels and 3.94 on average over 20 relabellings within cohort, range 2.98 to 6.58 (12_dispersion_reference.log). Binomial reads drawn from the model without ploidy and then scaled and rounded as normalizeCoverage does (12b_binomial_null.log, 5 x 3,000 CpGs): statistic inflated 1.19-fold and uncorrected p below 0.05, 0.01, 0.001 at 7.4%, 1.9%, 0.33%; unscaled 1.00 and 5.1%, 1.0%, 0.15%. The reference values themselves are reproduced by an independent simulation: medians 1.17 to 1.19 scaled and 0.96 to 0.98 unscaled (dispersion_summary.csv: 1.18 and 0.98). Scaling factors in library_filtering_legacy.csv: 1 to 1.31, mean 1.16.
discrepancies.proposed_text: 1. *Variation among libraries is about three times what binomial sampling gives, and the uncorrected test statistic is inflated nearly fourfold.* The dispersion estimate (Pearson chi-squared over residual degrees of freedom; 1 for binomial data; the quantity by which methylKit's correction divides the statistic) at 5,000 randomly chosen eligible CpGs has a median of 3.67 (quartiles 2.45 to 5.35) and exceeds 1.5 at 94% of them. Binomial reads simulated at the same coverage give 0.98, and 1.18 after the coverage scaling and rounding that step 05 applies. The uncorrected model refers its statistic to a chi-squared distribution, which assumes a dispersion of 1 whatever the scaling, so the statistic is inflated about 3.7-fold at a typical CpG: a factor of about 1.2 comes from the scaling of the counts (1.18 against 0.98) and a factor of about 3.1 from variation among libraries (3.67 against 1.18). One library was made per animal, so variation among animals and variation among library preparations cannot be told apart. In corrected mode: 3.59 for the observed counts, 0.99 for binomial reads and 1.19 after scaling and rounding (`dispersion_summary.csv`).

discrepancies.where: issues.md, I-06, item 7, first sentence
discrepancies.quote: With 11 libraries against 11, the correction, and 480,579 tests, a single CpG needs an F statistic above 84 (p below 2.1e-8) to be called on its own; with 5 against 5, above 474 (`dml_counts.csv`, column `statistic_needed_for_a_single_call`).
discrepancies.problem: The numbers are right (84.11, 474.47, 2.08e-8) but the statement holds only where the dispersion estimate is above 1. Where it is not, methylKit sets the estimate to 1 and uses the chi-squared test, so the 'corrected' p-value is the uncorrected p-value and a statistic of 31.4 is enough. Most of the corrected calls were made that way, so the sentence describes a hurdle that nearly all listed CpGs never had to clear. analyses.csv says this in its column reference_distribution; the issue text does not.
discrepancies.evidence: logReg (01_methylkit_source.out): phi = ifelse(phi > 1, phi, 1); test = ifelse(test == "F" & phi > 1, "F", "Chisq"). Recomputed thresholds: qf(0.01/480579, 1, 19) = 84.11; 1 and 18 df 89.51; 1 and 10 df 250.61; 1 and 8 df 474.47; qchisq 31.42, all equal to dml_counts.csv. Cached fits, corrected p identical to the uncorrected p of the matching fit (14_correction_not_applied.log): A1_ploidy_mn_f 1 of 2 DML (22 of the 24 with q < 0.01); A1_heat_mn_f 2 of 16 (142 of 287); A2_interaction_mn_f 2 of 2 (4 of 4); A4_ploidy_in_control_mn_f 2 of 2 (7 of 7); A4_ploidy_in_heat_mn_f 124 of 125 (219 of 220). Dispersion estimates recomputed at the calls (20_phi_at_corrected_calls.log): 0.54 at NC_047565.1:35,030,701 and 1.80 at NC_047562.1:40,685,928; 0.85 and 0.96 at the two control CpGs; not above 1 at 124 of the 125 heat-cohort CpGs (quartiles 0.64, 0.80, 0.91). Share of eligible CpGs with an estimate not above 1: 0.96% (22 libraries), 3.32% (controls), 6.12% (heat-treated).
discrepancies.proposed_text: With 11 libraries against 11, the correction, and 480,579 tests, a single CpG needs an F statistic above 84 (p below 2.1e-8) to be called on its own; with 5 against 5, above 474 (`dml_counts.csv`, column `statistic_needed_for_a_single_call`). This holds only where the dispersion estimate is above 1. Where it is not, methylKit sets it to 1 and refers the statistic to chi-squared with 1 degree of freedom, as in the uncorrected model (`analyses.csv`, column `reference_distribution`), and a statistic of 31.4 is enough. The estimate is not above 1 at 1.0% of the eligible CpGs with 22 libraries, 3.3% with the 12 controls and 6.1% with the 10 heat-treated libraries, and those CpGs supply most of the corrected lists: the corrected p-value equals the uncorrected one at 1 of the 2 ploidy CpGs, 2 of the 16 heat CpGs, both CpGs of the tested interaction, both CpGs among the controls and 124 of the 125 CpGs among the heat-treated (cached fits of `dml_sensitivity.R`; the script does not yet write these counts).

discrepancies.where: issues.md, I-06, 'Correction to "Why it matters" (2026-11-19)', first two sentences, against 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R lines 107 to 115
discrepancies.quote: the paper could not be opened from the audit environment (the publisher and the preprint server refused automated access). What that paper found and what it recommends are therefore unverified here
discrepancies.problem: The repository contradicts itself. The header of dml_sensitivity.R states what the benchmark found ('the default test without the correction had the lowest specificity and the best overall accuracy, the F test with the correction gave results similar to DSS, [...] the chi-squared test with the correction is named as a good compromise [...] three samples per group') and says it was 'read in the preprint version of August 2017, doi:10.1101/109512'. The issue log says the same paper could not be opened and that its content is unverified. One of the two statements is wrong, or the reading was made by one agent and never confirmed. If the header is right, a defender of the draft can cite the benchmark for the default test ('best overall accuracy'), and the log does not prepare the reader for that.
discrepancies.evidence: Europe PMC and Crossref answer for the DOI and confirm the metadata (Wreczycka K, Gosdschan A, Yusuf D, Gruning B, Assenov Y, Akalin A. Strategies for analyzing bisulfite sequencing data. J Biotechnol 2017;261:105-115; PMID 28822795; preprint PPR22834). From this session bioRxiv returned the full-text page (367 kB) and the PDF (2.9 MB) with HTTP 200 on the first request and HTTP 429 on seven later ones; ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403. I could not keep or read the content, so the account in the script header is neither confirmed nor refuted by this check.
discrepancies.proposed_text: the paper could not be read in the audit session (the publisher refused automated access and the preprint server answered only intermittently). What that paper found and what it recommends are therefore unverified in this log. The header of `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R` (note "Which of the two tests") gives an account of the benchmark as read in the preprint (doi:10.1101/109512): lowest specificity and best overall accuracy for the default test, results close to DSS for the F test with the correction, the chi-squared test with the correction as a compromise, three samples per group in the simulation. That account has not been confirmed by a second reading and is unverified in the same sense. Whatever the benchmark found, items 2, 4 and 7 below measure the three tests on these 22 libraries directly

discrepancies.evidence: united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz and united_cpg_corrected.csv.gz, row NC_047565.1:35030701 (05_locus_rows.txt): numCs/numTs of libraries 6 to 10 are 10/6, 11/13, 12/20, 10/14, 11/20, that is 62.5%, 45.8%, 37.5%, 41.7%, 35.5%; library 2 (zr3534_2) 2/27 = 6.9%; the 16 others 0 methylated reads. corrected_dml_library_values.csv prints the range as '35 to 62'.
discrepancies.proposed_text: All five heat-cohort triploids are 35.5% to 62.5% methylated there; 16 of the other 17 libraries are at 0% and one is at 6.9%

discrepancies.where: issues.md, I-06, item 4, sentence under the table
discrepancies.quote: The uncorrected lists grow as libraries are removed, because a pooled difference of 20 points is reached more easily by chance with fewer libraries.
discrepancies.problem: True of the relabelling medians, which the sentence does not cite, but not the whole reason for every row: the list of the heat-treated libraries is 3.2 times its relabelling median, and the two heat rows on 11 libraries have no reference at all. In the rows on fewer libraries the q-value criterion also removes CpGs, so those lists are not simply the CpGs above 20 points (item 3 says so only for the draft's two lists).
discrepancies.evidence: permutation_reference.csv, n_above_cutoff_median: 749 (22 libraries), 1,220.5 (18), 2,912.5 (12 controls), 4,019.5 (10 heat-treated), against observed 1,038; 1,214; 3,350; 13,028. dml_counts.csv, n_effect_above_cutoff against n_dml: 3,350 and 2,768 (controls), 13,028 and 12,405 (heat-treated), 12,964 and 12,487, 7,206 and 6,632 (heat among diploids, among triploids), 23,503 and 16,971 (interaction).
discrepancies.proposed_text: The uncorrected lists grow as libraries are removed, mostly because a pooled difference of 20 points is reached more easily by chance with fewer libraries: with relabelled libraries the median number of CpGs above 20 points is 749 with 22 libraries, 1,220.5 with 18, 2,912.5 with the 12 controls and 4,019.5 with the 10 heat-treated libraries (`permutation_reference.csv`). Only the list of the heat-treated libraries is longer than its reference (13,028 CpGs above 20 points; item 5 and the third point under "What follows"); the two heat rows on 11 libraries have no reference. In these smaller analyses the q-value criterion does remove CpGs: 582 of the 3,350 CpGs above 20 points among the controls, 623 of 13,028 among the heat-treated, and 6,532 of 23,503 for the interaction (`dml_counts.csv`, `n_effect_above_cutoff` against `n_dml`).

discrepancies.where: issues.md, I-06, Options, option 2
