discrepancies.problem: Contradicts item 5 of the same issue ('No reference of this kind can be built for the heat contrast'). A relabelling reference can stand beside the ploidy counts and the interaction count only.
discrepancies.evidence: permutation_reference.csv: the four heat rows of legacy mode and the heat row of corrected mode have n_labellings_possible = 1 and labellings_used = none.
discrepancies.proposed_text: Keep the uncorrected model and present its lists as descriptive, with the relabelling reference beside every ploidy count and the statement that no such reference exists for the heat contrast (item 5).

challenges.claim: Item 1: the dispersion estimate of the script (Pearson chi-squared over residual degrees of freedom) is the quantity that measures what the uncorrected model ignores.
challenges.objection: The script's estimator might not be the quantity by which methylKit's correction divides the statistic (different model, different degrees of freedom, different residuals).
challenges.test_done: Read methylKit:::logReg (1.28.0) and the vignette; rewrote the computation in base R (glm.fit, Pearson residuals of the full model ploidy + heat, 19 df, estimate floored at 1, F with 1 and 19 df where the estimate exceeds 1, else chi-squared) and compared with the cached fits at 3,000 sampled eligible CpGs (06_sample_and_parity.R) and with methylKit:::logReg itself at 300 of them.
challenges.result: Same formula: logReg computes sum(((y - w mu)/sqrt(mu (w - w mu)))^2)/(n - parameters), the script computes sum((y - n mu)^2/(n mu (1 - mu)))/df.residual on the same full model with 19 df; the vignette gives phi = X^2/(N - P). Largest relative difference of my p-values to cache/fit_A1_ploidy_mn_f_legacy.rds 1.2e-11 (MN chi-squared 1.2e-11, uncorrected 2.4e-11), to methylKit:::logReg 6.9e-13; for the two within-cohort corrected fits the p-values are identical to the cache. Only difference: methylKit sets estimates below 1 to 1 (0.8% of my sample, 0.9% of the script's). My sample: median 3.72, quartiles 2.52 and 5.57, 94.2% above 1.5 (script: 3.67, 2.45, 5.35, 94%).

challenges.claim: Item 1: 'so 1.18 is the value to compare with. The test statistic of the uncorrected model is thus inflated about threefold at a typical CpG.'
challenges.objection: 1.18 is the right comparison for how much of the dispersion comes from the libraries, but the wrong one for the inflation of the test statistic, whose reference distribution assumes 1.
challenges.test_done: Independent simulation of the two reference values; null simulation of binomial reads through the scaling of step 05; inflation of the uncorrected statistic measured directly with real and relabelled labels (12_dispersion_reference.R, 12b_binomial_null.R).
challenges.result: Reference values reproduced (1.17 to 1.19 and 0.96 to 0.98). Binomial reads with no group difference, scaled and rounded: statistic inflated 1.19-fold, 7.4%, 1.9%, 0.33% of p below 0.05, 0.01, 0.001. Observed counts: median statistic 3.90 times the chi-squared median (3.94 over 20 relabellings). So the inflation is 3.7 to 3.9, of which 1.2 from scaling and 3.1 from the libraries.
challenges.proposed_text: The uncorrected model refers its statistic to a chi-squared distribution, which assumes a dispersion of 1 whatever the scaling, so the statistic is inflated about 3.7-fold at a typical CpG: a factor of about 1.2 comes from the scaling of the counts (1.18 against 0.98) and a factor of about 3.1 from variation among libraries (3.67 against 1.18).

challenges.claim: Item 2 (heading and text under the table): 'With the correction, the ploidy contrast of the draft and the ploidy contrast among the controls have nearly the p-value distribution of groups that do not differ.'
challenges.objection: The comparison with 5%, 1%, 0.1% assumes that methylKit's corrected F test holds its level on these data. If it is conservative, 5.7% is a real excess; if anticonservative, the excesses of the other rows shrink.
challenges.test_done: Two independent random samples of 3,000 eligible CpGs of united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz; ploidy labels reassigned within cohort 150 times for each sample (300 relabellings); for each, methylKit's p-value for overdispersion "MN", test "F", heat as covariate, computed in base R (parity with the cache 1.2e-11). Same for the uncorrected test and MN chi-squared. Inside each cohort: all 125 other groupings of the 10 heat libraries, 150 of the 461 other groupings of the 12 controls (07, 08, 10, 18, 19 in my folder).
challenges.result: Corrected F test under relabelling, shares below 0.05, 0.01, 0.001: first 30 relabellings 5.2%, 1.06%, 0.11% (sample a) and 5.6%, 1.15%, 0.12% (sample b); all 300: mean 5.62%, 1.22%, 0.14%, median 4.88%, 0.93%, 0.10%, 5th to 95th percentile 3.5% to 9.3% at 0.05, maximum 19.7%. For the 234 relabellings with two exchanges in the heat cohort: 5.09%, 1.02%, 0.11%. So the test holds its level on average. Real labels at the same CpGs: 6.13%, 1.10%, 0.13% and 5.73%, 1.30%, 0.13% (full data 5.74%, 1.24%, 0.14%); 78, 95 and 119 of the 300 relabellings give at least as much. The share of one grouping depends on where it puts the five high-level libraries of I-49: mean 7.6% below 0.05 when four or five are in one group (107 relabellings), 4.5% when split three to two (193). Among the 163 relabellings with two exchanges in the heat cohort and a three to two split the mean is 4.4%, 0.85%, 0.09% and 4 reach the share of the real labels (descriptive, not a test). Controls: all 150 regroupings mean 5.4%, 1.03%, 0.14%; 70 regroupings with the two high control libraries in one group 6.6%, 1.2%, 0.16% (21 at or above the real grouping at 0.05), 80 that separate them 4.4%, 0.88%, 0.13% (none reaches it). Heat cohort: none of the 125 other groupings reaches the real 17.4% (largest 16.7%). Uncorrected test under relabelling: 33.2%, 21.0%, 11.8%, equal to the real labels (33.4%, 21.1%, 11.7%).
challenges.proposed_text: These nominal shares hold on average over groupings, not for each grouping, because the libraries are not alike (I-49). With the ploidy labels reassigned within cohort (300 relabellings, each at 3,000 eligible CpGs), the uncorrected test gives 33%, 21% and 12% on average, the same as with the real labels, and the corrected F test gives 5.6%, 1.2% and 0.14% on average, with 3.5% to 9.3% below 0.05 in nine relabellings of ten. With the correction, the ploidy contrast of the draft has the p-value distribution of relabelled libraries: 78 of the 300 relabellings give at least the share below 0.05 that the real labels give at the same CpGs (95 at 0.01, 119 at 0.001). The share depends mostly on where a grouping puts the five libraries of I-49: 7.6% below 0.05 on average when four or five of them fall into one group, 4.5% when they are split three to two. The ploidy contrast among the controls is of the same kind: its 6.7% is what regroupings give that keep the two high control libraries in one group, as the real grouping does (mean 6.6% over 70 such regroupings, 21 of them at or above the real grouping; 4.4% over the 80 that separate the two). The ploidy contrast inside the heat cohort and the interaction keep an excess that relabelling does not give: none of the 125 other groupings of the ten heat-treated libraries reaches 18%, and 1 of the 300 relabellings reaches the 20% of the interaction. The cohort contrast cannot be relabelled; 12 of the 300 relabellings of the ploidy label reach its 11%, so for that contrast the table shows less than the PCA does (I-44). What these differences consist of is described in I-49. (Relabelling figures: check S1-I06-numbers-and-reading, files `10_combine_relabel.log`, `18_level_by_kind_of_relabelling.log`, `08_relabel_level_within_cohort.log` and `19_control_regroupings_by_high_libraries.log`; not yet written by a repository script.) Heading of the item: *The uncorrected p-values are not usable, and the corrected ones show no ploidy signal that is common to the two cohorts.*

challenges.claim: Item 2, heading: 'The uncorrected p-values are not usable'.
challenges.objection: A share of 33% below 0.05 could be real ploidy signal and not miscalibration.
challenges.test_done: Uncorrected test under the same 300 relabellings; null simulation of binomial reads through the scaling of step 05.
challenges.result: Relabelled libraries give 33.2%, 21.0%, 11.8% on average (5th to 95th percentile at 0.05: 26.9% to 42.5%); 122, 117 and 110 of the 300 relabellings give at least the shares of the real labels. Binomial reads with no group difference already give 7.4%, 1.9%, 0.33% because of the scaling.

challenges.claim: Item 2: 'The cohort contrast, the ploidy contrast inside the heat cohort and the interaction keep an excess of small p-values: those groups of libraries do differ, at many CpGs'.
challenges.objection: An excess over the nominal 5% also arises from arbitrary groupings when libraries are heterogeneous, so 11%, 18% and 20% need a relabelling reference before they show a difference.
challenges.test_done: Same relabelling runs; interaction test (ploidy x heat against ploidy + heat, MN, F with 18 df) under the 300 relabellings; all 125 other groupings of the heat cohort.
challenges.result: Heat cohort: 0 of 125 other groupings reach the real share at any of the three levels (exact p = 1/126). Interaction: relabelled mean 5.8%, 1.3%, 0.14%; 1 of 300 relabellings reaches the real 19% to 20%. Cohort contrast: cannot be relabelled; as a yardstick, 12, 12 and 9 of the 300 relabellings of the ploidy label reach 11%, 3.6%, 0.67% (4 of the 234 with two exchanges in the heat cohort).
challenges.proposed_text: The ploidy contrast inside the heat cohort and the interaction keep an excess that relabelling does not give: none of the 125 other groupings of the ten heat-treated libraries reaches 18%, and 1 of the 300 relabellings reaches the 20% of the interaction. The cohort contrast cannot be relabelled; 12 of the 300 relabellings of the ploidy label reach its 11%, so for that contrast the table shows less than the PCA does (I-44).

challenges.claim: Item 5 (heading and text): 'The draft's ploidy list is no longer than lists made from relabelled libraries. [...] A grouping of the same animals that has nothing to do with ploidy thus yields about 750 "DML", and more than one such grouping in ten yields more than the real one.'
challenges.objection: (a) The reference counts CpGs above 20 points without the q criterion, so it may not be the statistic of the draft's list. (b) 113 of 1,000 includes the observed labelling and may include ties. (c) The relabellings that exceed the real count may not be groupings unrelated to ploidy: some keep most of the real grouping, some separate the five high-level libraries. (d) A defender would ask for relabellings balanced in those libraries.
challenges.test_done: Recomputed the reference with the labellings of the audit script (same seed and sampling code) on all tested CpGs, both modes (09_permutation_reference.R); classified each labelling by exchanges in the heat cohort and by the split of the five high-level libraries (17); hybrid labellings with one cohort at its real labels and the other regrouped in every way; complete enumeration of the 4,410 labellings that keep the five high-level libraries at their real labels (21); uncorrected p-values at relabelled CpGs above 20 points (11).
challenges.result: Reproduced exactly: 1,038 observed; median 749; 5th and 95th percentile 522.95 and 1,235.15; 113 of 1,000 with the observed labelling included, that is 112 of 999 random ones, all 112 strictly above 1,038 (corrected mode: 137 of 1,000; 135 of 999 strictly above, 1 equal). Same statistic, same libraries, cohort and group sizes kept; 999 of the 1,000 labellings distinct, none equal to the observed one or its mirror image. (a) holds: 99.98% of the relabelled CpGs above 20 points have an uncorrected p below 2.3e-4, the largest p with q < 0.01 in the draft's ploidy fit. (c) does not hold as written: of the 112 exceeding relabellings, 73 keep the real grouping of the heat cohort or change it by one exchange (202 of the 999 do), and 34 of the other 39 put four or five high-level libraries into one group; of the 571 that do neither, 5 reach 1,038 (median 677). With the heat cohort at its real labels, 903 of the 924 regroupings of the controls give at least 1,038 (median 1,530); with the controls at their real labels, 40 of the 252 regroupings of the heat cohort do (median 754). (d) Complete enumeration with the five high-level libraries fixed: median 740.5, 509 of 4,410 at or above 1,038, p = 0.115, the same as the random reference. Nothing in permutation_reference.csv contradicts the numbers of the text; the rows it does not cite are 18 libraries (1,214 against 1,220.5; 505 of 1,000), controls (3,350 against 2,912.5; 242 of 924) and interaction (23,503 against 9,379; 1 of 1,000).
challenges.proposed_text: Heading: *The draft's ploidy list cannot be told apart in length from lists made from relabelled libraries.* Replacement for the sentence that begins 'A grouping of the same animals': A random regrouping of the same animals thus yields about 750 "DML", and more than one regrouping in ten yields more than the real grouping (112 of the 999 random ones; 135 in corrected mode). These regroupings are not unrelated to the real one: 73 of the 112 keep the real grouping of the heat cohort or change it by a single exchange of two libraries (202 of the 999 do), and 34 of the other 39 put four or all five of the libraries of I-49 into one group. Of the 571 regroupings that do neither, 5 reach 1,038 (median 677). With the heat cohort at its real labels, 903 of the 924 regroupings of the controls give at least 1,038 (median 1,530); with the controls at their real labels, 40 of the 252 regroupings of the heat cohort do (median 754). The length of the list is therefore what the real grouping of the heat cohort gives (third point under "What follows"), reduced by the real grouping of the controls. A complete enumeration that keeps the five libraries of I-49 at their real labels gives the same answer as the random relabellings (509 of 4,410 labellings reach 1,038; median 740.5). (Check S1-I06-numbers-and-reading, files `09_permutation_reference_legacy.log`, `17_crosstab_permutation.log` and `21_stratified_enumeration.log`; not yet written by a repository script.)

challenges.claim: Item 6: 'The corrected heat list is therefore not stable at its threshold.' with the counts 157 of 287, 138 mitochondrial, none above 20 points, q from 0.0045 to 0.0094 rising to 0.010 to 0.020, Benjamini-Hochberg 15 and 4.
challenges.objection: The scratch counts might be miscopied; the ten CpGs might have left the list because they are not tested in corrected mode.
challenges.test_done: Recomputed from cache/fit_A1_heat_mn_f_legacy.rds and cache/fit_A1_heat_mn_f_corrected.rds with positions from the two united tables (04_item6.R).
challenges.result: All confirmed. 287 with q < 0.01 in legacy mode; 157 removed by the filter, 138 of them on NC_001276.1 (all 138 significant mitochondrial CpGs are removed; 363 mitochondrial CpGs tested in legacy mode, none kept), largest difference among the 157 is 12.2 points. All ten CpGs are in the corrected table with identical p-values; q 0.00449 to 0.00943 in legacy mode, 0.01030 to 0.01955 in corrected mode. All 130 retained significant CpGs: 84 still below 0.01. Benjamini-Hochberg: 15 and 4 DML. SLIM q is 0.913 (legacy) and 0.904 (corrected) times the Benjamini-Hochberg q.

challenges.claim: Item 6: 'A CpG at which one group of animals is uniformly different from all others is what an allele or a sequence variant shared by related animals produces in bisulfite data (I-08, I-49).'
challenges.objection: A defender reads the same pattern (methylated only in heat-treated triploids) as the ploidy by heat effect the draft claims.
challenges.test_done: Per-library counts read from both united tables; checked whether the call depends on the correction; no alignments are available, so genotype cannot be called.
challenges.result: Values confirmed (62.5%, 45.8%, 37.5%, 41.7%, 35.5% in the five heat triploids; 6.9% in zr3534_2; 0 of 13 to 31 reads in the 16 others). The dispersion estimate at this CpG is 0.54, so methylKit applied no correction: its 'corrected' p-values (1.8e-17 ploidy, 3.8e-22 heat) are the uncorrected ones. It is not called inside the heat cohort alone (q = 0.06). Whether it is an allele cannot be decided from counts.
challenges.proposed_text: A CpG at which one group of animals is uniformly different from all others is what an allele or a sequence variant shared by related animals produces in bisulfite data (I-08, I-49); it is also what a methylation difference confined to heat-treated triploids would produce, and the counts cannot tell the two apart. At this CpG the dispersion estimate is 0.54, so the correction was not applied and the corrected p-values are the uncorrected ones (item 7).

challenges.claim: Item 7: 'A short corrected list is therefore not evidence that two groups are alike at every CpG. It is evidence that these data cannot name the CpGs at which they differ. Item 2 is the better guide to whether groups differ at all.'
challenges.objection: Fair on power, but it treats the corrected list as a trustworthy lower bound. If the corrected test also calls CpGs for arbitrary groupings, a corrected list is not evidence of difference either.
challenges.test_done: Thresholds recomputed from analyses.csv residual df; t equivalents; corrected calls counted under relabelling at the p threshold of each observed list and at p < 0.01/480,579 (15, 15b).
challenges.result: Thresholds confirmed (84.11, 89.51, 250.61, 474.47; chi-squared 31.42). An F of 84 with 1 and 19 df is a t of 9.2, reached when two groups of 11 lie 3.9 within-group standard deviations apart; for 6 against 6 the figures are 15.8 and 9.1, for 5 against 5 they are 21.8 and 13.8. So the power statement is fair. But relabelled libraries are called too: 22 libraries, median 0 calls, 8 of 200 relabellings with 2 or more, 0.14 per relabelling below 2.1e-8; controls, median 2, 95 of 150 regroupings with 2 or more, 2.2 per regrouping below 2.1e-8; heat cohort, median 10 (5th to 95th percentile 4 to 41, largest 69) against 125 with the real labels, 5.4 per regrouping below 2.1e-8 (3.9 for the 100 groupings two exchanges away). Expected below 2.1e-8 under a test that holds its level: 0.01.
challenges.proposed_text: A short corrected list is therefore not evidence that two groups are alike at every CpG, and a corrected list is not a list of established differences either. These data cannot name the CpGs at which groups differ. Item 2, read against relabelled libraries, is the better guide to whether groups differ at all.

challenges.claim: What follows, Ploidy: 'The 1,038 ploidy DML cannot be reported as differences between diploid and triploid oysters. Lists of that size arise from arbitrary groupings of these animals (item 5), the corrected test finds nearly the p-value distribution of no difference (item 2) [...] This removes the basis of Results 3.2 to 3.5 as far as they concern ploidy'.
challenges.objection: Defender: (1) q < 0.01 with a difference threshold and the default model is the practice of the methylKit vignette; (2) the corrected F test has little power with 11 per group, so 2 survivors prove nothing; (3) pooling two cohorts with a covariate is legitimate; (4) most of the 1,038 are differences inside the heat cohort, where the audit itself says the groups differ.
challenges.test_done: (1) vignette read. (2) corrected p-values at the 1,038 against the CpGs above 20 points of 150 relabellings (11); lists at q < 0.05 and q < 0.1 (13). (3) hybrid labellings and the tested interaction under relabelling. (4) within-cohort pooled differences and within-cohort fits at the 1,038 (13).
challenges.result: (1) True: the vignette calls calculateDiffMeth(meth) with defaults and getMethylDiff(difference = 25, qvalue = 0.01). The text does not say so. (2) Power does not explain it: of the 1,038, 782 (75.3%) have a corrected p below 0.05, 278 (26.8%) below 0.01, 48 (4.6%) below 0.001; relabelled lists give 71.6%, 28.3%, 4.7% on average, and 27, 66, 48 of 150 relabellings give at least the real share. Median dispersion at the 1,038 is 6.57 (relabelled lists 6.16; typical eligible CpG 3.67). With q < 0.05 the corrected test calls 3 ploidy CpGs above 20 points, with q < 0.1 it calls 6. (3) With the heat cohort at its real labels, 903 of 924 regroupings of the controls give at least as long a pooled list; the interaction is beyond relabelling (1 of 300). (4) True and not said in this bullet: 880 of the 1,038 exceed 20 points with the same sign inside the heat cohort, 335 inside the control cohort, 179 in both; 860 are DML of the heat-only fit, 300 of the control-only fit, 139 of both. Of all 751 CpGs that are DML in both within-cohort fits, 139 have the same sign. The conclusion that the list has no support as a list of ploidy loci stands; 'arbitrary groupings' and 'cannot be reported as differences' say more than that.
challenges.proposed_text: - *Ploidy.* The 1,038 ploidy DML cannot be reported as loci that differ between diploid and triploid oysters, in general or "under control conditions". A list of that length cannot be told apart from the lists of relabelled libraries (item 5), with the correction its p-values are those of relabelled libraries (item 2), and the ploidy difference of one cohort is not found in the other (I-01, I-49). What the list mostly holds is the difference between the two ploidy groups of the heat experiment (third point): 860 of the 1,038 are DML among the heat-treated libraries alone and 300 among the controls alone (`dml_counts.csv`, analyses A4, column `n_in_primary`), 139 in both. That difference is real at the level of the groups, but its CpGs cannot be named: of the 125 CpGs called there with the correction, 7 are among the 1,038. Results 3.2 to 3.5 are therefore without support where they present ploidy DML as loci that differ by ploidy: Table 1, Figures 2 to 9 where they show ploidy DML, and the "interaction" set that is built from the ploidy list (I-02). The draft's settings are those of the methylKit vignette (default model, q < 0.01 and a difference threshold), so this is a finding about what common practice gives on these 22 libraries, not about an error of execution.

challenges.claim: What follows, Ploidy inside the heat cohort: 'Diploids and triploids of the heat experiment differ: 12,405 DML uncorrected, 125 corrected, and the number of CpGs above 20 points (13,028) is the largest that any of the 252 relabellings of those ten libraries gives.'
challenges.objection: The count may not single out the ploidy grouping, and '125 corrected' may be read as 125 established loci.
challenges.test_done: permutation_reference.csv and library_methylation_level/relabelling_small_sets.csv; corrected F shares and corrected calls under all 125 other groupings (08, 15); dispersion estimates at the 125 (20).
challenges.result: The group difference stands by three statistics: count above 20 points 13,028 against a median of 4,019.5 (2 of 252, the smallest share possible); corrected F share 17.4% against at most 16.7% in 125 other groupings; 125 corrected calls against at most 69. But the runner-up grouping (zr3534_1 and zr3534_6 exchanged) gives 12,822 CpGs above 20 points, and groupings that keep the three high diploid libraries together give 10% to 13% of corrected p below 0.05. The 125 are not established loci: 124 were tested without the correction (dispersion estimate not above 1; diploids and triploids do not overlap at 124), other groupings give a median of 10 such calls, 122 remain under Benjamini-Hochberg, 7 are among the draft's 1,038, and 101 of the 125 are lower in triploids.
challenges.proposed_text: - *Ploidy inside the heat cohort.* The diploid and the triploid libraries of the heat experiment differ as groups: the number of CpGs above 20 points (13,028) is the largest that any of the 252 relabellings of those ten libraries gives, although the grouping that exchanges zr3534_1 and zr3534_6 gives nearly as many (12,822; `library_methylation_level/relabelling_small_sets.csv`). The two list sizes, 12,405 uncorrected and 125 corrected, do not count established loci: relabelled libraries give a median of 4,019.5 CpGs above 20 points (`permutation_reference.csv`) and about ten corrected calls (item 7), and 124 of the 125 were tested without the correction because their dispersion estimate is not above 1. I-49 describes the difference: three diploid libraries with a higher overall methylation level, and five triploid libraries that resemble each other. Whether heat produced it cannot be decided without WGBS of that experiment's own control animals.

challenges.claim: What follows, Heat: 'The experiments do differ (item 2; I-44), but which CpGs differ cannot be named: 16 CpGs pass with the correction, 6 with the coverage filter.'
challenges.objection: A defender may say 16 named CpGs, or 185 with the chi-squared form, are a list.
challenges.test_done: Stability of the 16 under the filter and under Benjamini-Hochberg (04); corrected p-values at the draft's 2,351 heat DML (13); level of the chi-squared form under relabelling (10) and from the F distribution.
challenges.result: 16, 6, 15 and 4 confirmed. Of the draft's 2,351 heat DML, 82.0% have a corrected p below 0.05, 43.1% below 0.01, 11.9% below 0.001, above the 95th percentile of relabelled ploidy lists (79.7%, 36.6%, 10.1%), which agrees with 'the experiments do differ'. With q < 0.05 the corrected test calls 55 heat CpGs, with q < 0.1 it calls 125. The chi-squared form gives 7.2%, 2.2%, 0.47% under relabelling and is about 1,000 times too liberal at the p needed for a single call, so its 185 are not a list either.

challenges.claim: Options, option 1: 'Make the corrected model primary and report what it supports: no list of ploidy loci, no list of heat loci [...] This is the option the evidence supports.'
challenges.objection: The evidence supports reporting no list; it does not show that methylKit's corrected test is a sound primary analysis. If it were primary, its own lists (2, 16 or 6, 125) would have to be reported at face value.
challenges.test_done: Corrected calls under relabelling and the share of calls made without the correction (14, 15, 15b).
challenges.result: The corrected test leaves the test uncorrected at CpGs with a dispersion estimate not above 1; relabelled libraries get 0.14 (22 libraries), 2.2 (controls) and 5.4 (heat cohort) calls per relabelling below p = 2.1e-8, where 0.01 is expected. The recommendation 'no list' is supported more strongly than the text says; 'make the corrected model primary' is not supported without this caveat.
challenges.proposed_text: 1. Report no list of loci. With variation among animals modelled, these data support no list of ploidy loci and no list of heat loci, and a difference between the ploidy groups of the heat cohort that is described at the level of libraries (I-49). This is the option the evidence supports. The evidence is the relabelling references together with the corrected test; methylKit's corrected test is not by itself a calibrated primary analysis, because it leaves the test uncorrected wherever the dispersion estimate is not above 1 (item 7).

additions.item: The corrected lists are not lists with 1% false discoveries: relabelled libraries are called by the same corrected test, and nearly all calls are made at CpGs where methylKit applied no correction.
additions.why_it_matters: Items 4, 6 and 7 and the third point of 'What follows' present 2, 16 (6) and 125 as what survives a stringent test, and option 1 proposes that test as the primary model. An author could answer by reporting the 125 CpGs of the heat cohort or the 16 heat CpGs as validated loci. Under regrouping of the same libraries the procedure still returns about 10 calls in the heat cohort and 2 among the controls, so the q-values of the corrected lists do not mean what they say.

additions.proposed_text: The corrected lists are therefore not lists with 1% false discoveries. With the ploidy labels reassigned, the same test still calls CpGs above 20 points. CpGs with p below 2.1e-8, which have q < 0.01 whatever the other CpGs do and of which 0.01 per analysis is expected if the test held its level there, number 0.14 per relabelling on average with 22 libraries (median 0), 2.2 among the controls (median 2) and 5.4 among the heat-treated libraries (median 4). At the p-value threshold of each observed list the relabelled libraries give a median of 0 calls with 22 libraries (8 of 200 relabellings give 2 or more, the number called with the real labels), a median of 2 among the controls (95 of 150 regroupings give 2 or more), and a median of 10 among the heat-treated libraries (5th to 95th percentile 4 to 41, largest 69, over all 125 other groupings of the ten libraries; real labels 125). These calls come from CpGs whose dispersion estimate is not above 1 (80% of them with 22 libraries, all of them among the controls, 99.9% among the heat-treated). The two CpGs among the controls are what regrouped controls give. The list of 125 is longer than any regrouping gives, so the two groups of the heat cohort differ, but about ten such calls arise from an arbitrary grouping of those ten libraries. (Check S1-I06-numbers-and-reading, files `15_corrected_lists_heat.log`, `15b_corrected_lists_pooled_control.log` and `14_correction_not_applied.log`; not yet written by a repository script.)

result.notes:
Scope and state of the text. Checked: issues.md, I-06, from "**Rating.**" to "**Needs from authors.**", as it stood with md5 4419afee681fa01cbcd5faaa73c7be94 (the text changed once during the check: item 3 now names the one heat CpG of legacy mode, 2,352 above 20 points against 2,351 DML; that sentence is correct, the CpG is NC_047567.1:31,559,118, q = 0.0179, difference -20.35). Nothing under the repository was written; all scripts, logs and tables are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/S1-I06-numbers-and-reading/ (index in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/S1-I06-numbers-and-reading/README_check.txt). The proposed texts name my files as "check S1-I06-numbers-and-reading, <file>"; they are not repository files yet.

(a) Numbers. Every count, share and table cell of items 1 to 7 and of "What follows" was recomputed from the cached fits and the united tables and agrees with dml_counts.csv, permutation_reference.csv, dispersion_summary.csv and the DML list files (03_numbers_from_cache.log: all 22 fits, counts identical, shares equal to 5e-16). Eligible CpGs 65,480 and 61,056. Item 6 scratch counts all confirmed (see the challenge on item 6). No number in the checked text is wrong; the discrepancies are of reading, placement, order and rounding.

(b) Quotations. Both are word for word in methylKit 1.28.0. The first is in the entry of the argument overdispersion. The second is in the Details section and in the vignette, not in the entry of the argument test (low discrepancy above). The help page cites "McCullagh and Nelder. (1989). Generalized Linear Models. Chapman and Hall."

(c)2 in one sentence: under relabelling the corrected F test holds its level on average (5.6%, 1.2%, 0.14% over 300 relabellings; 5.1%, 1.0%, 0.11% for relabellings far from the real heat-cohort grouping), single groupings scatter between 3.5% and 9.3% at the 0.05 level, and the row of the real ploidy labels lies inside that scatter; but in the far tail, where the corrected lists are made, the test is not calibrated at all (high-severity addition).

Limits of what I did. The relabelling of p-value shares used two samples of 3,000 eligible CpGs in legacy mode, not all 65,480 and not corrected mode. The breakdowns by "exchanges in the heat cohort" and by the split of the five high-level libraries are descriptions of which relabellings reach the observed value; they are not tests, because they condition on closeness to the observed labelling. The two valid references for the list length are the random one (p = 0.113) and the complete enumeration with the five libraries fixed (p = 0.115). Corrected calls under relabelling were counted at fixed p thresholds (that of the observed list, and 0.01/480,579), not with q-values recomputed for each relabelling. In my file 12_dispersion_reference.log the columns "share p <" of the simulated rows are not null shares (reads were drawn from the full model there); the null simulation is 12b_binomial_null.log.

Could not check. The content of Wreczycka et al. 2017 (metadata confirmed through Europe PMC and Crossref; full text not obtained, see the medium discrepancy). Whether NC_047565.1:35,030,701 is a sequence variant (needs alignments). A relabelling reference for the cohort contrast (does not exist). The statement that the script was reviewed by a second agent before the full run. Metadata of the two DSS citations in option 3 agree with Crossref (Feng, Conneely, Wu 2014, Nucleic Acids Res 42(8):e69; Park and Wu 2016, Bioinformatics 32(10):1446-1453); their content was not read.

Same wording outside the checked section, to be changed in step if the proposals are taken: summary table row of I-06 (issues.md line 37, "The ploidy list is no longer than lists from relabelled libraries"); 07_documentation/reproducibility_plan.md item 15 ("about three times what it assumes", "no longer than"); 06_diagnostics/README.md, "How to read the size of a list", point 6 ("The model of the draft assumes the dispersion of the second row, not exactly 1" is wrong: the model assumes 1) and point 4 (the F threshold applies only where the dispersion estimate is above 1); header note of 06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R lines 166 to 175 (same point) and lines 107 to 115 (account of the benchmark).

One observation not followed up: the dispersion estimate does not rise with coverage in my sample (Spearman 0.016; medians 3.6 to 3.9 in all four coverage quartiles), which a constant between-animal correlation would predict. It does not affect any conclusion here.

challenges.proposed_text: **Update 2026-11-19 (computed; `06_diagnostics/library_methylation_level/corrected_dml_library_values.csv` and `corrected_dml_group_apart.csv`).** The CpGs that methylKit's corrected test calls (I-06) were looked at library by library. At nearly all of them the test applied no correction, because the dispersion estimate is not above 1 (I-06, items 6 and 7), so these are CpGs at which the libraries of each group agree closely. At NC_047565.1:35,030,701, the only CpG in both corrected lists of the draft's contrasts, all five heat-cohort triploids are 35.5% to 62.5% methylated and the other 17 libraries are at 0% (one at 7%). Of the 125 CpGs called for ploidy inside the heat cohort, 11 have all five triploids outside the range of the other 17 libraries, and 6 have all five diploids outside it. "Outside the range" is a weak criterion: at 12 of the 17 the group is separated from the nearest other library by less than 3.5 points, and at 5 (four with the triploids apart, one with the diploids apart) by 11 to 19 points; at all six diploid CpGs the diploids are the higher group, as their raised overall level gives (I-49). Over all 480,579 tested CpGs, whatever the test, the five heat-cohort triploids lie outside the range of the other 17 libraries at 98 CpGs (78 clusters at 1 kb), more than any other set of five heat libraries (median 14, largest 59); the five diploids do so at 34 CpGs, a number that 13 of the other 250 sets reach. With a margin of more than 10 points the counts are 14 for the triploids (largest other set 8) and 2 for the diploids (computed once by the check S4-updates-and-cross-file from `united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz`; not yet written by a script of the repository). The heat-cohort triploids are therefore set apart at more CpGs than an arbitrary group of five libraries is, and the diploids are not. A group of animals that is uniformly different from every other animal, controls of the same ploidy included, is the pattern a shared allele or sequence variant gives. A main effect of ploidy or of heat would not give it; a response to heat confined to one ploidy would, because each of these two groups is the only one with its combination of ploidy and treatment. This is a description of a few CpGs, not a variant call; the alignments are needed for that. It adds to the question in I-49 whether the triploids of the heat experiment are one family.

challenges.claim: Header lines 88 to 92 and README point 1: the counts differ from dml_sensitivity/permutation_reference.csv (3,350 against 3,349 for the control cohort, medians 4,019.5 against 4,018.5 for the heat cohort) because that script counts without the margin, that is, because of CpGs at exactly 20 points.
challenges.objection: The differences could come from something else: the screening of CpGs in relabel_reference(), another floating-point formula, or another set of groupings.
challenges.test_done: Legacy mode, all 480,579 CpGs, no screening, every grouping of the two cohorts (252 and 924) from bit patterns, group sums by adding columns. Three counts per grouping: exact (5*|cb*na - ca*nb| > na*nb, integers), without margin (|100*(cb/nb - ca/na)| > 20, the arithmetic of methylKit and of dml_sensitivity.R lines 659 to 660 and 702), with the margin. Script scripts/indep_02_relabel.R; details scripts/task4_details.R; methylKit's own values from the cached fits fit_A4_ploidy_in_control_legacy.rds and fit_A4_ploidy_in_heat_legacy.rds.
challenges.result: The counts without margin reproduce permutation_reference.csv exactly: heat_only 13,028 observed, quantiles 2,721, 2,984, 3,340, 4,019.5, 4,911, 10,297, 13,028, 2 labellings at least observed; control_only 3,350, quantiles 1,726, 2,083, 2,413, 2,912.5, 3,360, 3,948, 4,749, 242. The exact counts reproduce relabelling_reference.csv: 13,028, minimum 2,720, 5th percentile 2,983, median 4,018.5, 95th percentile 10,297; 3,349, 1,725, 2,083, 2,912.5, 3,948, largest other 4,749. The two rules differ in 160 of 252 and 552 of 924 groupings, by 1 to 6 CpGs; the 1,148 CpG by grouping cases (416 CpGs) are all differences of exactly 20 points whose floating-point value is 20.000000000000004 or 20.000000000000007. In the observed control grouping it is one CpG, NC_047563.1:63152425 (77 of 110 pooled reads methylated in the diploids, 72 of 80 in the triploids, 70% against 90%); methylKit's cached value is 20.000000000000007, the script's difference() gives exactly 20. The observed heat grouping has 20 such CpGs, 19 evaluate to exactly 20 and one to 19.999999999999996, so both scripts give 13,028. The medians: sorted counts at positions 126 and 127 are 3,981 and 4,056 (exact) and 3,983 and 4,056 (without margin).

challenges.claim: Comment in relabel_reference(), lines 196 to 198: 'a CpG whose library values span no more than the threshold can never be counted. Dropping those CpGs changes no count.'
challenges.objection: The bound holds in exact arithmetic; the screen (span > cutoff) and the count are both made in floating point, and the span is taken over the libraries of the comparison only.
challenges.test_done: Proof: a pooled value is a read-weighted mean of the library values of its group, all weights positive (smallest numCs + numTs is 10), so both pooled values lie between the smallest and largest value among the libraries of the comparison (the code takes the span over `libs` only; libraries outside the comparison have zero columns in A and B). If the computed span is at most 20, the true difference is at most 20 plus rounding error (below 1e-13), which is below the margin of 1e-9, so above() is FALSE. Numerical check: counts of dropped CpGs that exceed 20 points, in each of the 5,917 groupings of each mode, under the exact rule and under a rule without margin (scripts/indep_02_relabel.R); the script's own function against exact counts grouping by grouping (scripts/relabel_function_on_real_data.R); a built counterexample (scripts/tests_edge_cases.R).
challenges.result: Real data: 0 dropped CpGs above 20 points in every grouping, both modes, under both rules; the function's counts equal the exact counts in all 5,917 groupings of each mode. The screen keeps 82,085, 89,060, 65,442, 79,213, 90,605 and 82,085 of 480,579 CpGs (legacy); 1,194 to 1,738 CpGs per comparison have a span of exactly 20. Counterexample for a rule without margin: every library of group a at 6/10 and every library of group b at 8/10 gives a span of exactly 20 (dropped) and a difference of 20.000000000000007, which '> 20' counts (50 of 50 built CpGs). The claim therefore holds because above() has a margin, not by itself.
challenges.proposed_text:
# A pooled group value lies between the smallest and the largest library
  # value of its group, so at a CpG whose library values span no more than the
  # threshold the difference cannot exceed the threshold by more than rounding
  # error (about 1e-13), far less than the margin of above(). Dropping those
  # CpGs therefore changes no count. This relies on the margin: with a plain
  # '> cutoff', a CpG whose groups sit at exactly 60% and 80% has a span of 20
  # and a computed difference of 20.000000000000007.

challenges.claim: Header lines 84 to 88: a margin of 1e-9 separates differences of exactly 20 points from all others, so n_exactly_at_threshold counts exact ties and nothing else is miscounted.
challenges.objection: Legacy mode has no upper coverage filter. With deep coverage two different pooled differences can lie closer than 1e-9, and then a difference that is truly above 20 would be reported as a tie.
challenges.test_done: For two groups the distance of a difference from 20 is 20*|5*|cb*na - ca*nb| - na*nb| / (na*nb), so the smallest nonzero distance is 20/(na*nb). Largest product of pooled reads over all contrasts and all groupings; exact integer classification of every contrast and grouping against the script's; for the interaction (four denominators, no such bound) exact fractions for every CpG within 1e-6 of 20 (scripts/indep_01_contrasts.R, indep_02_relabel.R, python fractions).
challenges.result: Legacy: up to 10,335 reads in one library, 57,590 and 57,711 pooled reads in the two ploidy groups (NC_047567.1:36952059), product 3.32e9, smallest possible nonzero distance 6.0e-9 (9.5e-9 in the groupings of part 6); corrected mode: at most 111 reads per library, 4.5e-5. Observed: the nearest difference that is not a tie is 0.00032 points from 20; floating-point error at ties at most 7.1e-15. n_exactly_at_threshold equals the exact number of ties in all 16 rows (0, 1, 20, 8, 1, 31, 6, 9 in both modes). The single interaction candidate (NC_047561.1:51291786) is an exact tie (-20). So nothing is miscounted now; the margin is 6 times below the smallest distance the legacy data allow, and a product of pooled reads above 2e10 would break the guarantee.

code_findings.problem: combn(c(s$a, s$b), length(s$a)) is called on the vector of library indices. When a stratum holds a single library, combn() reads the single number x as 1:x and enumerates libraries that are not in the stratum. An empty group is not caught either.
code_findings.failure_scenario: None at current settings (strata hold 5, 7, 10 or 12 libraries). With strata {1,2 | 3,4} and {7 | none} the function returns 42 groupings instead of 6, among them group a = (1,1,2), and stopifnot(sum(is_observed) == 1) at line 217 passes. With an empty group a it returns the count NA without a message. Both arise if the gap rule leaves one library of a cohort or removes a whole group.
code_findings.proposed_fix: per_stratum <- lapply(strata, function(s) { x <- c(s$a, s$b); stopifnot(length(s$a) >= 1, length(s$b) >= 1); combn(length(x), length(s$a), FUN = function(i) x[i], simplify = FALSE) })

code_findings.problem: The screen keep <- which(span > cutoff) is safe only because above() requires a margin of 1e-9; the comment at lines 196 to 198 states it without that condition. The README announces that the code pass will give both scripts one rule; if that rule has no margin the screen starts to change counts. n_cpg_screened is returned and written nowhere.
code_findings.failure_scenario: None at current settings: in both modes no dropped CpG exceeds 20 points in any of the 5,917 groupings, with or without the margin. With a rule '> cutoff' and a CpG at which every library of one group is at 6/10 and every library of the other at 8/10: span = 20 exactly (dropped), difference = 20.000000000000007 (counted by the unscreened rule); 50 of 50 built CpGs in tests_edge_cases.R.
code_findings.proposed_fix: Reword the comment (text under challenges) and make the screen independent of the rule: keep <- which(span > cutoff - 1e-6). Write n_cpg_screened to relabelling_reference.csv or drop it.

code_findings.problem: One quantity is computed in two floating-point forms: difference() (lines 170 to 171) gives 100*cb/nb - 100*ca/na, relabel_reference() (line 211) gives 100*(cb/nb - ca/na), which is methylKit's form. At differences of exactly 20 points the two forms round differently, so the two paths agree only through the margin of above() (lines 135 to 136). The check against step 05 at line 248 accepts 1e-8, ten times the margin.
code_findings.failure_scenario: None at current settings: the ten rows shared by contrast_direction.csv and relabelling_reference.csv are equal. Without the margin, legacy mode: difference() would give 10,733 and 3,191 for the two contrasts without the high libraries where the matrix form gives 10,732 and 3,190, and 3,349 and 3,994 (control cohort, acute heat shock) where the matrix form gives 3,350 and 3,995. With the margin a wrong count needs two different differences within 1e-9, possible once the product of the pooled reads of two groups exceeds 2e10 (largest now 3.32e9 in legacy mode, which has no upper coverage filter) and never excluded for the interaction contrast, which has four denominators.
code_findings.proposed_fix: Decide on the pooled counts without division, in both scripts: above <- 100 * abs(cb * na - ca * nb) > cutoff * na * nb; tie <- 100 * abs(cb * na - ca * nb) == cutoff * na * nb; with stopifnot(100 * max(na) * max(nb) < 2^53) (exact in double precision; largest value now 3.3e11). Keep the margin for the interaction and stop if any value lies between 1e-9 and 1e-6 from the cutoff. I ran this rule on every contrast, every left-out library and every grouping of both modes: no number of the 13 tables changes. Applied to dml_sensitivity.R it changes permutation_reference.csv (legacy): control_only n_effect_above_cutoff 3,350 to 3,349, minimum 1,726 to 1,725, q25 2,413 to 2,412, q75 3,360 to 3,358; heat_only minimum 2,721 to 2,720, q05 2,984 to 2,983, q25 3,340 to 3,339, median 4,019.5 to 4,018.5, q75 4,911 to 4,910; and n_effect_above_cutoff of A4_ploidy_in_control in dml_counts.csv (the CpG is not a DML, so no list changes); the rows with 1,000 random labellings were not recomputed.

discrepancies.problem: One-sided. The first half holds: the article reports the lowest specificity and the highest false positive rate for the default test. The second half does not hold as worded: the article recommends by purpose, not one test. It rates the default test best in overall accuracy (highest F-score) and accepts it for exploratory analysis, names DSS, limma and the F test with the correction for work that must limit false positives, and calls the chi-squared test with the correction a compromise between the two. The page range is 105-115.
discrepancies.evidence: Article read in full in the publisher's version (PDF metadata: Journal of Biotechnology, 261 (2017) 105-115), open copy at https://edoc.mdc-berlin.de/16722/, saved as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/S5-literature/downloads/mdc/16722oa.pdf (this folder is written [S5] below) (sha256 53caa73bc4359bd64b661882016b25097dc105a98cfdb18973685e6f6c42fe74), text in [S5]/text/wreczycka2017_mdc16722_raw.txt. Sections 4.1, 4.2 and 9; verbatim sentences under citations. Figure 2b measured from the embedded 300 dpi image ([S5]/scripts/measure_fig2_bars.py, output [S5]/text/fig2_bar_measurements.txt): specificity of the default test 0.68 to 0.71 over the five effect sizes, chi-squared test with the correction 0.93 to 0.95, F test with the correction 0.98 to 0.99, DSS and limma 0.99 to 1.00. The F-score panel equals the F1 score computed from the measured sensitivity and specificity with 2,500 changed and 2,500 unchanged CpGs to within 0.006 at all 22 measurable bars (0.002 at the five bars of the default test; [S5]/text/fig2_f1_identity_check.txt), which validates the readings.
discrepancies.proposed_text: The methylKit authors' own benchmark reports the lowest specificity and the highest false positive rate for the default test without the correction. It also reports the highest F-score for that test, which it calls the best overall accuracy, accepts the default test for exploratory analysis, names the stringent tests (DSS, limma and methylKit's F test with the correction) for work that must limit false positives, and calls the chi-squared test with the correction a good compromise between the two (Wreczycka et al. 2017, J Biotechnol 261:105-115, doi:10.1016/j.jbiotec.2017.08.007).

discrepancies.where: issues.md, I-06, paragraph "**Correction to "Why it matters" (2026-11-19).**", sentences "What that paper found and what it recommends are therefore unverified in this log." and "That account has not been confirmed by a second reading ..."
discrepancies.quote: That account has not been confirmed by a second reading and is unverified in the same sense; an author with access to the journal should check it.
discrepancies.problem: Stale after this check. The article was read in full: all four points of the account in the script header are confirmed in the published version, and no journal access is needed (the article is open access, CC BY-NC-ND, and an open copy is in the repository of the Max Delbrück Center). The sentence "What that paper found and what it recommends are therefore unverified in this log." of the same paragraph is stale for the same reason. Point 1: "MethylKit without overdispersion showed the lowest specificity (the overdispersion correction usually improves specificity)." (4.1); "MethylKit without overdispersion had the highest F-score (Fig. 3c), but also the lowest specificity." and "although it is still the best method when overall accuracy is considered" (4.2); "A very relaxed method, such as the default methylKit method, has the best accuracy overall but highest false positive rate." (9). Point 2: "F-test with overdispersion has similar results to DSS" (4.1). Point 3: "We believe that a good compromise between the DSS/limma/F-test and default methylKit test is the overdispersion corrected methylKit Chi-square test." (4.1); "A good compromise between stringent and relaxed methods seems to be Chi-squared test with overdispersion correction." (4.2). Point 4: "We simulated a dataset consisting of 6 samples (3 controls and 3 samples with treatment)." (4.1). The methylKit help text quoted in the paragraph was compared with the installed methylKit 1.28.0 ([S5]/text/methylkit_help.txt) and is exact.
discrepancies.proposed_text:
**Correction to "Why it matters" (2026-11-19; the article was read the same day).** The sentence on the benchmark of Wreczycka et al. 2017 was written from memory and is one-sided. The check of the citations then read the article in the publisher's version (J Biotechnol 261:105-115; open copy in the repository of the Max Delbrück Center, https://edoc.mdc-berlin.de/16722/). The publisher's site and the preprint server refused automated access, so the preprint (doi:10.1101/109512) was not compared. What the article reports, in its sections 4.1, 4.2 and 9:
- *Design of the benchmark.* A simulation of six samples, three per group, with sets of 5,000 CpGs in each of which half were changed by 5, 10, 15, 20 or 25 points, called at q < 0.01 without a difference threshold; and RRBS data of 19 cell lines with two replicates each. No comparison is between groups that do not differ.
- *The default test.* "MethylKit without overdispersion showed the lowest specificity (the overdispersion correction usually improves specificity)." In the simulation it called about 30% of the unchanged CpGs, against 5% to 7% for the chi-squared test with the correction, 1% to 2% for the F test with the correction and at most 1.5% for DSS and limma (bar heights of its Figure 2b, the article prints no numbers; `fig2_bar_measurements.txt` in `07_documentation/agent_workflows/verification_scripts/S5-literature/`, measured once by the check of the citations). It also had the highest F-score, and the article concludes that the default method "has the best accuracy overall but highest false positive rate". With half of the CpGs changed, that score rewards sensitivity.
- *The corrected tests.* "F-test with overdispersion has similar results to DSS". The article does not recommend one test. The default test "can be used for more exploratory analysis"; limma, DSS and the F test with the correction "can be applied when there is a need to limit false positive rates, such as when picking regions or CpGs for validation"; and "A good compromise between stringent and relaxed methods seems to be Chi-squared test with overdispersion correction."

The account in the header of `06_diagnostics/dml_sensitivity.R` (note "Which of the two tests") is confirmed on its four points: lowest specificity and best overall accuracy for the default test, results close to DSS for the F test with the correction, the chi-squared test with the correction as a compromise, three samples per group in the simulation. The original sentence was right about the false positive rate; it left out that the same article rates the default test best in overall accuracy and accepts it for exploratory work. That rating does not carry over to these data: it rests on comparisons in which half of the CpGs truly differ, whereas here the ploidy list cannot be told apart in length from lists of relabelled libraries (item 5). Items 2, 4 and 7 below measure the three tests on these 22 libraries directly. Item 4 finds that the chi-squared form does not hold its level here, which is in line with the 5% to 7% of unchanged CpGs that it called in the benchmark at q < 0.01. Also verified is the documentation of methylKit 1.28.0 (`?calculateDiffMeth`): for `overdispersion`, "If set to "none"(default), no overdispersion correction will be attempted. If set to "MN", basic overdispersion correction, proposed by McCullagh and Nelder (1989) will be applied"; in the Details section (and in the vignette, section "Correcting for overdispersion"), "If overdispersion correction is applied, the function automatically switches to the F-test. The Chisq-test can be manually chosen in this case as well". The help page cites the correction as McCullagh and Nelder (1989), *Generalized Linear Models*, Chapman and Hall.
